definition_zh: 想象中的；虚构的；假想的
definition_en: existing only in the mind and not in the real world
core_image: 小孩在纸上画出一只会飞的鹿，它只活在纸上
scene: 孩子们常在纸上画出不存在的朋友。The dragon in her story is entirely imaginary.
sceneCN: 这里 imaginary 是「虚构的」（第 1 个义项：只存在于想象中）；句意是她故事里的龙完全是虚构的。

pos.zh: 形容词：想象中的；虚构的；假想的

derivatives.zh: 由 imagine 加 -ation 构成，义为「想象、想象力」

senses.title: Existing only in the mind
senses.titleCN: 虚构的：只存在于脑海中
senses.definition: existing only in someone's mind and not in physical reality
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于某人脑中，现实中并不存在
senses.example: The dragon in her story is entirely imaginary.
senses.exampleCN: 她故事里的龙完全是虚构的。
senses.why: The Latin suffix -arius builds an adjective from image, so the word names things that belong to images rather than to the world.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁后缀 -arius 由 image 造出形容词，因此这个词命名的是「属于图像的东西」，而不是现实中的东西。

senses.title: Invented for a story or game
senses.titleCN: 假想的：为故事或游戏而造
senses.definition: created by an author or player as part of a fiction
senses.definitionCN: 由作者或玩家作为虚构内容创造出来
senses.example: The children invented an imaginary country with three rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们编造了一个有三条河的假想国家。
senses.why: Fiction is the most natural home of the word: what is made up is precisely what was never seen.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品是这个词最自然的家：编造出来的东西，恰恰是从未见过的。

senses.title: A line drawn for reasoning
senses.titleCN: 假想的：为推理画出的辅助线
senses.definition: a line or point used in geometry although nothing physical is there
senses.definitionCN: 几何中使用但现实中没有实体的线或点
senses.example: Draw an imaginary line from the pole to the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 从杆子到岸边画一条假想的线。
senses.why: Geometry needs objects that nobody can touch, so it borrows this word for its tools.
senses.whyCN: 几何需要没人能摸到的对象，于是借这个词来称呼它的工具。

senses.title: A fear with no real cause
senses.titleCN: 臆想的：并无真实缘由的
senses.definition: a worry or threat that exists only in a person's mind
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于某人头脑中的担忧或威胁
senses.example: Most of his imaginary illnesses disappeared after the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 他大部分臆想的病在考试之后都消失了。
senses.why: The word can turn inward and describe what the mind itself manufactures to fear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以转向内心，描述头脑自己制造出来的恐惧。

senses.title: In mathematics, involving the root of a negative
senses.titleCN: 虚数的：数学中涉及负数的平方根
senses.definition: in mathematics, relating to a number whose square is negative
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，与平方为负数的数有关
senses.example: An imaginary number cannot be placed on the ordinary number line.
senses.exampleCN: 虚数无法放在普通的数轴上。
senses.why: Mathematicians named these numbers by what they are not: they are called imaginary because no ordinary quantity fits.
senses.whyCN: 数学家按这些数「不是什么」来命名：它们被称为虚数，因为没有普通量与之对应。

intro.en: Imaginary comes from Latin imaginarius, belonging to an image, from imago, a likeness.
intro.cn: imaginary 来自拉丁语 imaginarius「属于图像的」，源于 imago「相似的像」。

items.en: Imago meant a likeness, a copy, or a picture of a thing.
items.cn: imago 意为「相似的像、复制品、某物的图像」。

items.en: The verb imaginari meant to picture something in the mind.
items.cn: 动词 imaginari 意为「在心中勾画出某物」。

items.en: Scholars used imaginarius for what belongs to a mental picture.
items.cn: 学者用 imaginarius 指「属于心中图像的东西」。

items.en: French imaginaire carried the word toward fiction and fancy.
items.cn: 法语 imaginaire 把词推向虚构与幻想。

items.en: English took imaginary for things that exist only in thought.
items.cn: 英语借 imaginary 指只存在于思想中的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the imag- stem; the near-meaning group holds words about unreal things and about creative minds.
note.cn: 形近组共用 imag- 词干；近义组收表示「不真实」与「有创造力」的词。

entries.definition: The power or act of forming pictures in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「想象力、想象」。

entries.definition: Good at creating new ideas or pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富有想象力的」。

entries.definition: To form a picture of something in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「想象」，与 imaginary 同根。

entries.definition: Invented for a story rather than true.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚构的」，多指故事中的。

entries.definition: Not existing in fact, often as a judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不真实的」，常含判断意味。

entries.definition: To act as if something is true when it is not.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「假装」，与「真实」相对。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work with the imag- family, the word image and the geometry sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 imag- 词族、image 一词与几何用法。

normal.en: Image hides inside imaginary: an image that never leaves the paper.
normal.cn: image 藏在 imaginary 里面：一张始终没离开纸的图像。

normal.en: The ending -ary marks an adjective, so imaginary is the quality of an image, not the image itself.
normal.cn: -ary 是形容词后缀，所以 imaginary 是「图像的属性」，不是图像本身。

normal.en: Imaginable and imaginative sit on either side: one can be pictured, one can picture.
normal.cn: imaginable 与 imaginative 分居两侧：一个是「可被想象」，一个是「善于想象」。

normal.en: An imaginary line is a tool of geometry, drawn to help the eye reason.
normal.cn: an imaginary line 是几何工具，画出来帮眼睛推理。

normal.en: An imaginary friend is a real comfort to the child, even though nobody else sees it.
normal.cn: imaginary friend 对孩子是真实的安慰，尽管别人看不见。

abstract.en: What is imaginary has no weight, no address and no witness.
abstract.cn: 虚构之物没有重量，没有地址，也没有证人。

abstract.en: Every plan begins imaginary, and only work makes it exist.
abstract.cn: 每个计划起初都是虚构的，只有劳作让它存在。

abstract.en: A line that is only drawn is still useful when it helps the proof arrive.
abstract.cn: 只是画出来的线，只要能让证明抵达，就仍然有用。

examples.en: The beast in the novel is imaginary, but the fear is real.
examples.cn: 小说里的野兽是虚构的，但恐惧是真实的。

examples.en: Teachers sometimes draw an imaginary circle on the floor.
examples.cn: 老师有时会在地板上画一个假想的圆圈。

examples.en: Children often talk to an imaginary companion.
examples.cn: 儿童常跟想象中的伙伴说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一马金」——梦里的金马，一碰就散，只是想象中的马。

root: 拉丁语 imago（像、图像）+ -arius（形容词后缀）→ imaginarius；同族词有 image、imagine、imagination、imaginative。

sensesIntro.en: Imaginary names whatever belongs to an image rather than to the world, and its senses spread from stories to geometry and to the mind's own fears.
sensesIntro.cn: imaginary 命名一切属于图像而非属于世界的东西，义项从故事一路铺到几何与内心的恐惧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flying deer on a sheet of paper, real only to the pencil.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸上一只会飞的鹿，只对铅笔为真。

branches.en: MIND LINE: the thing exists in thought alone.
branches.cn: 心智线：事物只存在于思想中。

branches.en: STORY LINE: a writer gives the unreal a plot.
branches.cn: 故事线：作者给不真实之物一个情节。

branches.en: TOOL LINE: geometry draws what nobody can hold.
branches.cn: 工具线：几何画出没人能握住的东西。

branches.en: FEAR LINE: the mind invents its own threat.
branches.cn: 恐惧线：头脑自己造出威胁。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: mathematics names what ordinary numbers cannot reach.
branches.cn: 数线：数学命名普通数达不到的东西。

intro.en: A Latin stem for image, an adjective ending, and a family of words about picturing.
intro.cn: 一个表「图像」的拉丁词干、一个形容词词尾，加一族与「勾画」有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin imago gave imaginari, to picture, and imaginarius, belonging to a picture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 imago 生出 imaginari「在心中勾画」与 imaginarius「属于图像的」。

items.example: The stem of image and imagination.
items.exampleCN: image 与 imagination 的词干。

items.example: It turns a noun stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词词干变成形容词。

definition_en: to copy the way someone or something acts, sounds or looks
core_image: 小孩跟在大人身后，一抬手一抬脚地学样子
scene: 小孩最喜欢跟在大人后头学动作。Parrots can imitate human speech surprisingly well.
sceneCN: 这里 imitate 是「模仿」（第 1 个义项：学别人说话或动作）；句意是鹦鹉模仿人说话能出奇地像。

pos.zh: 动词：模仿；仿效；仿制

derivatives.zh: 由 imitate 加 -ion 构成，义为「模仿、仿制品」
加 in- 表否定，义为「无法模仿的」

senses.title: To copy a voice or action
senses.definition: to copy the way a person speaks or moves
senses.definitionCN: 照着某人说话或动作的样子去做
senses.example: A few students can imitate the teacher's accent perfectly.
senses.exampleCN: 有几个学生能惟妙惟肖地模仿老师的口音。
senses.why: Latin imitari already meant to copy, and copying a living person is the first use a child finds for it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 imitari 本就意为「复制」，而摹仿一个活人是孩子在生活里最先用到的场景。

senses.title: To follow a model as a guide
senses.definition: to behave in the way a respected person behaves
senses.definitionCN: 按照受尊敬之人的样子去做
senses.example: Young players imitate the habits of their heroes.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻球员仿效偶像的习惯。
senses.why: Copying here turns from sound to conduct: what is imitated is a way of living.
senses.whyCN: 这里的复制从声音转向行为：被仿效的是一种生活方式。

senses.title: To copy the look of something
senses.definition: to make a thing that looks like another thing
senses.definitionCN: 做出外观与另一物品相似的物品
senses.example: The factory imitates the design but uses cheaper parts.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂仿制了外观，却用了更便宜的零件。
senses.why: From copying a person it is a short step to copying an object made by that person.
senses.whyCN: 从摹仿一个人，到摹仿他做出的物品，只差一步。

senses.title: To take on the appearance of
senses.definition: to look or sound like something else by nature
senses.definitionCN: 在自然状态下显出与另一事物相似的样子
senses.example: Some insects imitate leaves so well that birds pass them by.
senses.exampleCN: 有些昆虫把叶子仿拟得极像，鸟都飞过去了。
senses.why: Nature herself copies: the verb lets a harmless creature borrow another thing's face.
senses.whyCN: 大自然自己也在复制：这个词让无害的生物借用别的形象。

senses.title: To mimic for fun
senses.definition: to copy someone in order to amuse others
senses.definitionCN: 为了逗别人开心而学某人
senses.example: He imitated his boss at dinner and everyone laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 他在晚饭时学老板的样子，大家都笑了。
senses.why: The same act can serve two moods, respect or mockery, and English keeps both under one verb.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作可以服务于两种心情，尊敬或嘲弄，英语把它们都收在同一动词下。

intro.en: Imitate comes from Latin imitari, to copy, through the adjective imitatus.
intro.cn: imitate 来自拉丁语 imitari「复制、仿效」，经形容词 imitatus 进入英语。

items.en: Imitari meant to copy or to represent something.
items.cn: imitari 意为「复制、再现」。

items.en: Some scholars connect it with imago, a likeness, though the link is debated.
items.cn: 一些学者把它与 imago「像」联系起来，但此说仍有争议。

items.en: Church writers used imitari for following the example of a holy life.
items.cn: 教会作家用 imitari 指「效法」圣洁生活的榜样。

items.en: French imiter carried the word into everyday use.
items.cn: 法语 imiter 把这个词带入日常使用。

items.en: English imitates voices, styles and products alike.
items.cn: 英语里既有模仿嗓音，也有模仿风格与仿制产品。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the imit- family; the near-meaning group separates copying, mocking and following by example.
note.cn: 形近组收 imit- 词族；近义组区分「复制」「嘲弄」与「效法」三种近义动作。

entries.definition: The act of copying, or a copy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「模仿、仿制品」。

entries.definition: Tending to copy others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「模仿的、模仿性的」。

entries.definition: So good that nobody can copy it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无法模仿的」。

entries.definition: To make something exactly like another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「复制」，最中性的说法。

entries.definition: To copy someone in a playful or mocking way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「模仿」，常带玩笑或嘲弄意味。

entries.definition: To try to equal someone by copying their effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「效仿」，偏向学习其努力。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the imit- family, the child's gesture and the insect that looks like a leaf.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 imit- 词族、孩子的动作与像叶子的昆虫。

normal.en: Imitate and image both begin with imi-, and both have to do with making a likeness.
normal.cn: imitate 与 image 都以 imi- 起头，都与「造像」有关。

normal.en: Add -tion and you get imitation, the action or the fake product.
normal.cn: 加上 -tion 就是 imitation，既指动作也指仿制品。

normal.en: In- plus imitable gives inimitable: the one thing nobody can imitate.
normal.cn: in- 加 imitable 得到 inimitable：无人可仿的那一种。

normal.en: An imitator copies; an inventor starts from nothing.
normal.cn: imitator 复制，inventor 从无到有。

normal.en: Parrots imitate sounds because their tongues are shaped for it.
normal.cn: 鹦鹉能学人声，是因为舌头的形状适合。

abstract.en: Copying is the fastest way for a beginner to learn and the slowest way to become original.
abstract.cn: 模仿是新手学得最快的方式，也是通往独创最慢的路。

abstract.en: A likeness made sincerely becomes homage; made to laugh, it becomes mockery.
abstract.cn: 真诚造出的相像是致敬，为了逗笑则是嘲弄。

abstract.en: Nature imitates itself endlessly, and human imitators are only keeping pace.
abstract.cn: 自然无止境地模仿自己，人的仿效只是跟着走。

examples.en: Children imitate what they see far more than what they hear.
examples.cn: 孩子模仿看到的，远多于模仿听到的。

examples.en: The parrot imitated the ring of the phone.
examples.cn: 那只鹦鹉模仿电话铃声。

examples.en: No painter should merely imitate another painter.
examples.cn: 任何画家都不该只去模仿另一位画家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一米踢他」——学别人的样子，一米的距离也要踢他一脚，纯属学样。

root: 拉丁语 imitari（复制、仿效）+ -atus → imitatus；同族词有 imitation、imitative、imitator、inimitable。

sensesIntro.en: Imitate copies a voice, a conduct, an object, a shape or a joke, and the five senses mark whom the copy is serving.
sensesIntro.cn: imitate 复制的是嗓音、行为、物品、外形或玩笑，五个义项区别就在于这份复制在为谁服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child stepping in the footprints of an adult.
core.cn: 核心意象：小孩踩着大人的脚印走。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: the sound is copied exactly.
branches.cn: 声音线：声音被一模一样地复制。

branches.en: MODEL LINE: a respected person sets the pattern.
branches.cn: 榜样线：受尊敬的人定下范式。

branches.en: PRODUCT LINE: a maker copies another maker.
branches.cn: 产品线：制作者复制另一个制作者。

branches.en: NATURE LINE: appearance is borrowed by instinct.
branches.cn: 自然线：外观靠本能借用。

branches.en: FUN LINE: the copy is performed for laughter.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：复制是为了逗笑。

intro.en: A Latin verb of copying, a noun ending for its act and an in- form for what cannot be copied.
intro.cn: 一个表「复制」的拉丁动词、一个指动作的名词词尾，以及一个表「不可复制」的否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin imitari, to copy, became imitatio and the English verb imitate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 imitari「复制」生出了 imitatio，也生出了英语动词 imitate。

items.example: The stem of imitation and imitative.
items.exampleCN: imitation 与 imitative 的词干。

definition_en: extremely large in size, amount or degree
core_image: 站到海边，视线一直到天边也看不到岸
scene: 船驶出港口，四周只剩水和天。The desert stretched out before them, immense and silent.
sceneCN: 这里 immense 是「浩瀚的、巨大的」（第 1 个义项：空间上极大）；句意是沙漠在他们面前铺开，浩瀚而寂静。

pos.zh: 形容词：巨大的；极大的；浩瀚的

derivatives.zh: 由 immense 加 -ity 构成，义为「广大、浩瀚」

senses.title: Enormous in size
senses.definition: extremely large in physical size
senses.definitionCN: 在物理体积上极大
senses.example: An immense rock blocked the entrance to the cave.
senses.exampleCN: 一块巨大的岩石堵住了洞口。
senses.why: Latin im- means not and mensus means measured, so immense first meant beyond measuring.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 im- 表否定、mensus 表「量过的」，所以 immense 本义是「量不完的」。

senses.title: Huge in amount
senses.definition: very great in quantity or sum
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或总额上极大
senses.example: The project needed an immense amount of steel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要数量惊人的钢材。
senses.why: The same negative prefix attaches to a sum instead of a length, and the word shifts from metres to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 同一个否定前缀从长度挪到总额上，词义便从米转向了数字。

senses.title: Very strong in feeling or effort
senses.definition: very great in degree, such as pressure or effort
senses.definitionCN: 在程度如压力、用力上极大
senses.example: The team worked under immense pressure before the final.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在决赛前承受着巨大的压力。
senses.why: Pressure cannot be put on a ruler either, so degree joins size and number under one adjective.
senses.whyCN: 压力同样无法用尺子量，于是程度也和体积、数量一起落进同一个形容词。

senses.title: Widely admired or known
senses.definition: very great in reputation or public interest
senses.definitionCN: 在声望或公众关注上极高
senses.example: The novel enjoyed immense popularity in its first year.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说第一年就极受欢迎。
senses.why: Fame is also beyond counting, and English happily applies the word to it.
senses.whyCN: 声望也是数不完的，英语便乐于把这个词也用上去。

intro.en: Immense joins Latin in-, not, with mensus, measured: the unmeasured.
intro.cn: immense 由拉丁语 in-「不」与 mensus「量过的」组成：没被量完的。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure, the source of mensus.
items.cn: metiri 意为「测量」，是 mensus 的来源。

items.en: Immensus described space that could not be measured.
items.cn: immensus 形容无法测量的空间。

items.en: French immense carried the adjective toward size in general.
items.cn: 法语 immense 把这个形容词推向泛指的大小。

items.en: English applied immense to size, amount and degree.
items.cn: 英语让 immense 覆盖体积、数量与程度。

items.en: Everyday speech softened it into a mere intensifier.
items.cn: 日常口语把它弱化为单纯的加强语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the mens- root, measure; the near-meaning group lines up words from big to enormous.
note.cn: 形近组共用 mens-「测量」词根；近义组按从「大」到「极大」排列近义词。

entries.definition: The quality of being huge or endless.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广大、浩瀚」。

entries.definition: To a very great degree.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「极其」。

entries.definition: To find the size of something; from Latin mensura.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「测量」，与 immense 同根，词源为 mensura。

entries.definition: Very large, the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大的」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: Extremely wide and open, as of land or space.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辽阔的」，多指空间。

entries.definition: Extremely large, often with a sense of excess.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极大的」，常含「超常」意味。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the im- plus mens structure, the sea horizon and the business collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 im- 加 mens 的结构、海平面与商务搭配。

normal.en: Im- is not, mens is measured: immense is what the ruler gives up on.
normal.cn: im- 是不，mens 是量过：immense 就是尺子放弃的地方。

normal.en: Measure and immense share mens, so the word carries a hidden ruler.
normal.cn: measure 与 immense 共用 mens，这个词里藏着一把尺。

normal.en: Immensely is the adverb used for feelings: immensely grateful.
normal.cn: immensely 用来加强感受：immensely grateful。

normal.en: Immense pressure is a collocation you will meet in every workplace story.
normal.cn: immense pressure 是职场里到处都能见到的搭配。

normal.en: Immensity names the space that no number can finish.
normal.cn: immensity 命名的是任何数字都数不完的空间。

abstract.en: The unmeasured is not always the largest; sometimes it is only the furthest from a ruler.
abstract.cn: 量不完的不一定最大，有时只是离尺子最远。

abstract.en: Awe begins where counting stops.
abstract.cn: 敬畏始于计数停止之处。

abstract.en: Pressure feels immense because inner space has no units at all.
abstract.cn: 压力之所以显得巨大，是因为内心的空间根本没有单位。

examples.en: The immense hall was filled with the sound of a single violin.
examples.cn: 巨大的厅堂里只回荡着一把小提琴的声音。

examples.en: She took immense pleasure in teaching children to read.
examples.cn: 她在教孩子识字中得到极大的快乐。

examples.en: An immense effort went into rebuilding the bridge.
examples.cn: 重建这座桥投入了极大的努力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一门死」——门大得能把整条街的门都堵死，可见其巨大。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ mensus（量过的，来自 metiri 测量）→ immensus（无法测量的）；同族词有 immensity、immensely、measure、dimension。

sensesIntro.en: Immense began as unmeasured and now stretches over size, quantity, degree and fame.
sensesIntro.cn: immense 最初意为「量不完」，如今覆盖体积、数量、程度与声望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sea with no far shore in sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片看不到对岸的海。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: the body feels small beside it.
branches.cn: 空间线：在它旁边身体显得很小。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: the sum passes easy counting.
branches.cn: 数量线：总额超出了轻松可数的范围。

branches.en: FORCE LINE: pressure and effort press down hard.
branches.cn: 力度线：压力与努力沉重地压下来。

branches.en: REPUTATION LINE: public attention grows beyond measure.
branches.cn: 声望线：公众关注大到无法衡量。

branches.en: CONTRAST: what can be measured is merely big, not immense.
branches.cn: 对照线：能量出来的只是「大」，不是「巨大」。

intro.en: A negating prefix on the root for measuring, plus the family that grew around measure.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加在「测量」词根上，再加上围绕 measure 长出的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin metiri, to measure, gave mensus and immensus, the unmeasured.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」生出 mensus 与 immensus「无法测量的」。

items.example: It negates the participle that follows.
The stem of measure and dimension.
items.exampleCN: measure 与 dimension 的词根。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 无法测量的；无边无际的

definition_en: a person who comes to live permanently in a country that is not their own
core_image: 一个人提着旧皮箱走下船，脚下的土地不是出生的地方
scene: 码头上，人们提着行李四处张望。Her grandparents arrived as immigrants with almost nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 immigrant 是「移民（移入者）」（第 1 个义项：来到他国定居的人）；句意是她的祖父母几乎一无所有地作为移民来到这里。

pos.zh: 名词：移民；移居入境者

derivatives.zh: 由 immigrate 加 -ion 构成，义为「移民入境、移居」
换前缀，义为「移居出境者」

senses.title: A person who settles in a new country
senses.definition: someone who moves to another country in order to live there
senses.definitionCN: 为定居而搬到另一个国家的人
senses.example: Her grandparents arrived as immigrants with almost nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母几乎一无所有地作为移民来到这里。
senses.why: The prefix im- means into, so the noun names the person who has come in to stay.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 im- 表示「向内」，因此这个名词命名的是「进来定居的那个人」。

senses.title: A person from one region living in another
senses.titleCN: 外来者：从外地迁入的人
senses.definition: a person who has moved from another region or area
senses.definitionCN: 从别的地区迁入的人
senses.example: Many immigrants from the north settled along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 许多来自北方的移民在河边定居。
senses.why: The same person can be called an immigrant by the new town and an emigrant by the old one; the word only records the view from inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人在新地方被称为 immigrant，在老家则被称为 emigrant；这个词只记录从里面看的那一面。

senses.title: In biology, a plant or animal new to a place
senses.titleCN: 外来物种：生物学中迁入的动植物
senses.definition: a species that has moved into an area where it did not live before
senses.definitionCN: 迁入到原先并不生活的地区的物种
senses.example: The weed is an immigrant from another continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这种杂草是从另一个大陆来的外来物种。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the human word because a new plant also arrives on a ship or in a load of soil.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了人的说法，因为新的植物同样是随船或随一车泥土到达的。

intro.en: Immigrant comes from Latin immigrare, to move into, from in-, into, and migrare, to move.
intro.cn: immigrant 来自拉丁语 immigrare「迁入」，由 in-「进入」与 migrare「迁移」构成。

items.en: Migrare meant to move from one place to another.
items.cn: migrare 意为「从一个地方迁到另一个地方」。

items.en: Immigrare added in-, the direction into a new place.
items.cn: immigrare 加上 in-，方向指向迁入的新地方。

items.en: The participle immigrans named the one who was moving in.
items.cn: 分词 immigrans 指「正在迁入的人」。

items.en: French immigrant fixed the ending for the person.
items.cn: 法语 immigrant 为「人」这一含义固定了词尾。

items.en: English applied the word to settlement and later to biology.
items.cn: 英语让它先指移居定居，后来又用于生物学。

note.en: The look-alike group differs only in prefix: em-, im-, mi-; the near-meaning group separates words for people who move.
note.cn: 形近组只在前后缀上有别：em-、im-、mi-；近义组区分几个表示「迁徙者」的词。

entries.definition: A person who leaves their country to live elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「移居出境者」，方向与 immigrant 相反。

entries.definition: The process of people coming into a country.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「移民入境」。

entries.definition: A person or animal that moves from place to place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迁移者、候鸟」，方向不限。

entries.definition: A person who has recently arrived.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「新来者」，范围更宽。

entries.definition: Someone who makes a home in a new region, often said of pioneers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「定居者」，多指开拓者。

entries.definition: A person forced to leave home because of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「难民」，强调被迫离开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the im- plus migr structure, the ship dockside image and the biology sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 im- 加 migr 的结构、码头下船的意象与生物学用法。

normal.en: Im- is in, migr is move: immigrant is the one moving in.
normal.cn: im- 是「向内」，migr 是「移动」：immigrant 就是往里移动的人。

normal.en: Swap im- for e- and you get emigrant, the one moving out.
normal.cn: 把 im- 换成 e- 就是 emigrant，往外移动的人。

normal.en: Immigration is the process, immigrant is the person.
normal.cn: immigration 是过程，immigrant 是人。

normal.en: Migrant keeps no direction, so birds and workers both fit.
normal.cn: migrant 不表方向，所以鸟与工人都能说。

normal.en: A refugee is an immigrant who had no choice about leaving.
normal.cn: refugee 是没有选择余地的 immigrant。

abstract.en: To immigrate is to carry a whole past into an unwritten address.
abstract.cn: 移民入境，就是把整个过去搬进一个还没有写好的地址。

abstract.en: Every country is made of people who once arrived.
abstract.cn: 每个国家的居民，都是曾经抵达的人。

abstract.en: The word marks a direction, not a rank.
abstract.cn: 这个词只标记方向，不标记高低。

examples.en: Many immigrants opened small shops near the station.
examples.cn: 许多移民在车站附近开了小店。

examples.en: He is an immigrant who learned the language in two years.
examples.cn: 他是两年就学会当地语言的移民。

examples.en: The city grew quickly through immigrants from the countryside.
examples.cn: 这座城市靠乡下来的移民迅速扩张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「移民阁润特」——移民住进了阁楼，把生活的「润」色也带了过来。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ migrare（迁移）+ -ant（人）→ immigrans；同族词有 immigrate、immigration、migrant、emigrant、migrate。

sensesIntro.en: Immigrant names the person who has moved in, and its senses widen from a country to a region and to a species.
sensesIntro.cn: immigrant 命名「迁入的那个人」，义项从国家扩展到地区，再到物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a suitcase set down on unfamiliar ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧皮箱落在陌生的土地上。

branches.en: COUNTRY LINE: the person settles in a new nation.
branches.cn: 国界线：在另一个国家定居。

branches.en: REGION LINE: the border is internal, not national.
branches.cn: 地区线：边界在国内，而非国与国之间。

branches.en: NATURE LINE: plants and animals migrate too.
branches.cn: 自然线：动植物也会迁入。

branches.en: CONTRAST: emigrant looks out, immigrant looks in.
branches.cn: 对照线：emigrant 朝外看，immigrant 朝里看。

branches.en: FEELING LINE: arrival often means starting again.
branches.cn: 情感线：抵达往往意味着从头开始。

intro.en: A prefix of direction on the root for moving, finished with the ending that marks a person.
intro.cn: 方向前缀加「迁移」词根，最后以标记「人」的词尾收束。

latinIntro.en: Latin migrare, to move, produced immigrans, the one moving in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 migrare「迁移」产生了 immigrans「正在迁入的人」。

items.example: The stem of migrate and migrant.
items.exampleCN: migrate 与 migrant 的词根。

items.example: It turns a verb into a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指人的名词。

items.meaning: to move from place to place

definition_en: not following accepted standards of right and wrong behaviour
core_image: 一只脚踏过了众人默认的那条界线
scene: 大家都知道这条线不能越。Cheating on the test was not illegal, but it was immoral.
sceneCN: 这里 immoral 是「不道德的」（第 1 个义项：违背公认的是非标准）；句意是考试作弊不违法，但不道德。

pos.zh: 形容词：不道德的；违背道德的

derivatives.zh: 由 moral 加 -ity 构成，义为「道德、道德性」
由 immoral 加 -ity 构成，义为「不道德」
去掉否定前缀，义为「道德的」

senses.title: Against accepted moral standards
senses.titleCN: 不道德的：违背公认的是非标准
senses.definition: contrary to the moral standards accepted by most people
senses.definitionCN: 与大多数人接受的道德标准相违背
senses.example: Cheating on the test was not illegal, but it was immoral.
senses.exampleCN: 考试作弊不违法，但不道德。
senses.why: Latin in- before m- means not, so the word simply denies the moral quality of an act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 在 m 前变为 im-，意为「不」，这个词就是对一个行为的道德性直接说不。

senses.title: Willing to do wrong for gain
senses.titleCN: 品行不正的：为了利益不惜作恶
senses.definition: ready to act wrongly in order to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为了获取好处而愿意做错事
senses.example: An immoral seller had sold him a fake medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 一个不择手段的卖家卖给他假药。
senses.why: When the prefix lands on a person, it describes a habit of choosing wrong whenever it pays.
senses.whyCN: 当这个前缀落在人身上时，它描述的是一种「只要有利就选错」的习惯。

senses.title: Unacceptable in a shared code
senses.titleCN: 不合规矩的：违反行业或群体准则
senses.definition: against the code of a profession or group, not of the whole society
senses.definitionCN: 违背某个行业或群体的准则，而非全社会标准
senses.example: Copying a rival's files is considered immoral in journalism.
senses.exampleCN: 在新闻界，抄袭同行的稿件被视为不合规矩。
senses.why: Every trade keeps its own mores, so the same negation can be applied to a group smaller than a country.
senses.whyCN: 每个行业都有自己的 mores，所以同一个否定前缀也可以加在小于国家的群体上。

intro.en: Immoral is a modern build: Latin in-, not, plus moral, and it replaced the older unmoral.
intro.cn: immoral 是现代构词：拉丁语 in-「不」加 moral，取代了更早的 unmoral。

items.en: Mos, plural mores, meant custom, the habits of a community.
items.cn: mos 复数 mores 意为「习俗、群体的习惯」。

items.en: Moralis was coined for what concerns customs and conduct.
items.cn: moralis 是后来造的，指与习俗、行为规范有关。

items.en: English moral arrived for customs, then for right and wrong.
items.cn: 英语 moral 先指习俗，后指善恶。

items.en: The prefix in- was joined to moral to make immoral.
items.cn: 把前缀 in- 加到 moral 上，形成 immoral。

items.en: Speakers still feel the gap between immoral and illegal.
items.cn: 说话人仍能感到 immoral 与 illegal 之间的差别。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with the im-/in- negation on moral words; the near-meaning group contrasts immoral with unmoral, amoral and illegal.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 moral 词族与否定前缀；近义组把 immoral 与 unmoral、amoral、illegal 对照。

entries.definition: The quality of being immoral, or an immoral act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不道德、不道德行为」。

entries.definition: Concerned with right and wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「道德的」，即去掉否定前缀的本词。

entries.definition: Beliefs about right and wrong behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「道德、道德准则」。

entries.definition: Lacking any moral sense, rather than breaking rules.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「没有道德意识的」，与「违背道德」不同。

entries.definition: Against the rules of a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合职业道德的」。

entries.definition: Against the law, which is not the same as immoral.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「违法的」，与「不道德」并不等同。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the im- negation, the moral family and the line between law and ethics.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 im- 否定、moral 词族以及法律与伦理的界线。

normal.en: Im- is not, so immoral is the plain denial of moral.
normal.cn: im- 表「不」，所以 immoral 就是对 moral 的直接否定。

normal.en: Amoral is another matter: it means the person has no moral sense at all.
normal.cn: amoral 是另一回事：指人根本没有道德意识。

normal.en: Keep illegal beside immoral: one is broken law, the other broken faith.
normal.cn: 把 illegal 与 immoral 并排：一个违的是法，一个违的是信。

normal.en: Immorality is the noun; immorality is what a court of opinion judges.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 immorality，它由舆论的法庭来审。

normal.en: Moral came from mores, the customs a community shares.
normal.cn: moral 出自 mores，即群体共享的习俗。

abstract.en: Law can be obeyed and morality still broken.
abstract.cn: 守住了法，道德上仍可能失守。

abstract.en: The line is drawn by a community, so it moves when the community moves.
abstract.cn: 这条线由群体画出，所以群体一变，线也跟着动。

abstract.en: An immoral act is one that a person would be ashamed to explain aloud.
abstract.cn: 不道德的事，是一个人不好意思当众解释的事。

examples.en: It is immoral to sell a product you know is dangerous.
examples.cn: 明知产品有危险还出售，是不道德的。

examples.en: Some people thought the advertisement was immoral.
examples.cn: 有些人觉得那则广告不道德。

examples.en: The law said nothing, but the practice was widely held to be immoral.
examples.cn: 法律没有规定，但这种做法被普遍认为不道德。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一摸就坏」——一碰就坏了的规矩，说的是不道德的事。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不，在 m 前变 im-）+ moral（道德的，来自拉丁语 mos/mores 习俗）→ immoral；同族词有 moral、morality、immorality、amoral。

sensesIntro.en: Immoral denies the moral quality of an act, a person or a code, and the three senses differ in who set the standard.
sensesIntro.cn: immoral 否定行为、人的或群体准则的道德性，三个义项的区别在于标准由谁设定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot crossing a line that everyone sees but nobody drew.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚踏过人人都看见、却没人画出的线。

branches.en: SOCIETY LINE: the whole community judges the act.
branches.cn: 社会线：整个群体来评判这个行为。

branches.en: GAIN LINE: the motive is profit, not principle.
branches.cn: 利益线：动因是好处，而非原则。

branches.en: CODE LINE: a profession sets its own rules.
branches.cn: 行规线：某个行业自定律条。

branches.en: CONTRAST: illegal is narrower; immoral is broader.
branches.cn: 对照线：illegal 更窄，immoral 更宽。

branches.en: FEELING LINE: the act brings shame when named aloud.
branches.cn: 情感线：当众说出这件事会带来羞耻。

intro.en: A Latin negating prefix on the word for custom and conduct, beside its positive and its philosophical cousin.
intro.cn: 否定前缀加在「习俗与品行」这个词上，另有肯定形式与哲学术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin mores, customs, gave moralis; putting in- before it produced the modern immoral.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mores「习俗」生出 moralis，加上 in- 便成现代的 immoral。

items.example: It denies the quality named after it.
items.exampleCN: 它否定后面所指的性质。

items.example: The stem of moral and mores.
items.exampleCN: moral 与 mores 的词根。

items.example: It makes an adjective from a noun.

items.meaning: the sense of right and wrong

definition_en: a strong effect on someone or something, or the force of one object hitting another
core_image: 石子砸进水面，波纹一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 一块石头落进湖里，水面荡开层层波纹。The new road had a huge impact on the village.
sceneCN: 这里 impact 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对人或事产生的强烈作用）；句意是新修的路对村子影响很大。

pos.zh: 名词：影响；冲击；撞击
动词：影响；撞击

derivatives.zh: 义为「有显著影响的」，多用于现代写法
同根词改前缀，义为「紧凑的」

senses.title: A strong effect
senses.titleCN: 影响：对人或事产生的强烈作用
senses.definition: a strong and often immediate effect on something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物产生强烈且往往迅速的作用
senses.example: The new road had a huge impact on the village.
senses.exampleCN: 新修的路对村子影响很大。
senses.why: Latin impactus is the past participle of impingere, to drive in, so the noun first names a blow that lands and then the change it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 impactus 是 impingere「撞入」的过去分词，所以这个名词先指落在身上的那一击，再指它留下的变化。

senses.title: The force of a collision
senses.definition: the force with which one body strikes another
senses.definitionCN: 一个物体击中另一物体时的力量
senses.example: The impact of the fall broke two windows.
senses.exampleCN: 坠落的撞击震碎了两扇窗。
senses.why: The physical sense is the oldest one, and it still appears whenever the word is about bodies rather than ideas.
senses.whyCN: 物理义是最早的含义，只要涉及的不是观念而是物体，它仍然会浮现。

senses.title: The moment of hitting
senses.definition: the act or instant of one thing hitting another
senses.definitionCN: 一物撞上另一物的动作或瞬间
senses.example: The cars exploded on impact.
senses.exampleCN: 两车一撞上就起火了。
senses.why: The noun can also name the instant itself, which is why on impact is a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指那一瞬间本身，所以 on impact 成为固定短语。

senses.title: To press or drive something in
senses.definition: to fix something firmly into a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢嵌进某个表面
senses.example: The dentist impacted the crown into the gum line.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医把牙冠嵌进牙龈线。
senses.why: This sense goes back to the literal root: something is driven in and stays fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项回到字面词根：某物被击入并牢牢固定。

senses.title: A tooth stuck in the jaw
senses.definition: in medicine, a tooth that cannot come through the gum
senses.definitionCN: 医学上，牙齿无法正常穿出牙龈
senses.example: An impacted wisdom tooth often has to be removed.
senses.exampleCN: 阻生的智齿常常需要拔除。
senses.why: In medicine the same image turns inward: a tooth driven into the jaw and unable to come out.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里这同一幅画面转向体内：牙齿被顶进颌骨，出不来。

intro.en: Impact comes from Latin impactus, struck against, from pangere, to drive in or fix.
intro.cn: impact 来自拉丁语 impactus「撞上的」，源于 pangere「击入、钉入」。

items.en: Pangere meant to drive in, as a nail is driven into wood.
items.cn: pangere 意为「击入」，像钉子被钉进木头。

items.en: Impingere added in- and meant to strike against something.
items.cn: impingere 加上 in-，意为「撞向某物」。

items.en: The participle impactus named the state of having been struck.
items.cn: 分词 impactus 表示「已被撞上」的状态。

items.en: English took impact first as the force of a blow.
items.cn: 英语最初用 impact 指打击的力量。

items.en: The sense of a lasting effect on people spread from journalism.
items.cn: 「对人产生的持久影响」这一义项从新闻写作中扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pang- root or the impact- stem; the near-meaning group moves from effect to collision.
note.cn: 形近组共用 pang- 词根或 impact- 词干；近义组从「效果」排到「碰撞」。

entries.definition: Having been hit, pressed in, or blocked.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受影响的、嵌入的、阻生的」。

entries.definition: Having a strong effect, a modern adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有显著影响的」，是较新的说法。

entries.definition: An agreement between parties; spelled alike but from Latin pactum, not from pangere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协定」，只是拼写相近，词源为拉丁语 pactum，与 impact 并非同源。

entries.definition: A change caused by something, the neutral word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效果、结果」，最中性的说法。

entries.definition: A quiet power that shapes what others do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「影响力」，多指缓慢持久的作用。

entries.definition: One moving body striking another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碰撞」，强调物体相撞。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pang- root, the stone-in-water image and the reporting collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 pang- 词根、石子入水的意象与新闻搭配。

normal.en: Impact hides pact which looks familiar, but the real root is pangere, to drive in.
normal.cn: impact 里看着眼熟的 pact 是错觉，真正的词根是 pangere「击入」。

normal.en: Keep the stress in mind: the noun is IMpact, the verb often imPACT.
normal.cn: 注意重音：名词是「IMpact」，动词常读作「imPACT」。

normal.en: Have an impact on is the phrase to use for effects on people.
normal.cn: have an impact on 是表示「对人产生影响」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Environmental impact statements come before the building starts.
normal.cn: 环境影响的评估报告总是在动工之前。

normal.en: An impacted tooth is literally a tooth that cannot come through.
normal.cn: impacted tooth 字面上就是「穿不出来的牙」。

abstract.en: A blow lasts a second; its impact may last a generation.
abstract.cn: 一击只持续一秒，它的影响却可以持续一代人。

abstract.en: Impact needs a receiver, which is why both the blow and the change keep one name.
abstract.cn: impact 总要有个承受者，所以那一击与那变化共用同一个名字。

abstract.en: What strikes hardest often makes the least sound.
abstract.cn: 撞得最重的，常常声音最小。

examples.en: The strike had an impact on every household in the town.
examples.cn: 这次罢工影响了镇上的每一户人家。

examples.en: The impact of the ball broke the glass.
examples.cn: 球的撞击打碎了玻璃。

examples.en: Sound changes little even after a long impact.
examples.cn: 即使撞击时间很长，声音的变化也很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一拍克它」——一巴掌拍上去，冲击力把对方一下克住。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ pangere（击入、钉住）→ impingere → impactus；同族词有 impacted、impactful、compact、propagate（同源异支）。

sensesIntro.en: Impact moves from a physics blow to the wave it leaves, and the last senses keep the literal sense of something driven in.
sensesIntro.cn: impact 从物理的一击走向它留下的波纹，后两个义项仍保留「被击入」的字面义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone landing in still water, rings reaching the shore.
core.cn: 核心意象：石子落进静水，波纹一直推到岸边。

branches.en: EFFECT LINE: the blow becomes a long consequence.
branches.cn: 效果线：一击变成长期的后果。

branches.en: FORCE LINE: the crash itself, before any result.
branches.cn: 力度线：任何后果之前的碰撞本身。

branches.en: DENTAL LINE: something is pressed into place.
branches.cn: 嵌入线：某物被压进原位。

branches.en: MEDICAL LINE: a tooth is blocked below the gum.
branches.cn: 医学术语线：牙齿被阻在牙龈之下。

branches.en: CONTRAST: influence is slow, impact is sudden.
branches.cn: 对照线：influence 缓慢，impact 突然。

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin root for driving in, and the family of words about pressing and striking.
intro.cn: 方向前缀、表「击入」的拉丁词根，以及一族与「压、撞」有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pangere, to fix or drive in, gave impingere and its participle impactus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pangere「钉入、击入」生出 impingere 及其分词 impactus。

items.example: It directs the blow toward an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把撞击指向某个对象。

items.example: The stem of impact and compact.
items.exampleCN: impact 与 compact 的词根。

definition_zh: 不耐烦的；急躁的；急切的
definition_en: not able to wait calmly, or eager for something to happen soon
core_image: 手指在桌面上不断敲，眼睛一次又一次看向门口
scene: 等人等得太久，他开始不停看表。The children grew impatient as the bus was late.
sceneCN: 这里 impatient 是「不耐烦的」（第 1 个义项：无法耐心等待）；句意是公交车迟到，孩子们越来越不耐烦。

pos.zh: 形容词：不耐烦的；急躁的；急切的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀，义为「耐心」
本义为「有耐心的」，也可作名词指「病人」
由 impatient 加 -ence 构成，义为「不耐烦」

senses.title: Unable to wait calmly
senses.titleCN: 不耐烦的：无法心平气和地等
senses.definition: annoyed because something takes too long
senses.definitionCN: 因为事情拖得太久而烦躁
senses.example: The children grew impatient as the bus was late.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车迟到，孩子们越来越不耐烦。
senses.why: Latin pati means to suffer, so patience is the ability to bear a wait; in- turns that bearing into its absence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pati 意为「承受」，耐心即承受等待的能力；in- 把这份承受变成「承受不住」。

senses.title: Eager for something to happen
senses.titleCN: 急切的：盼着某事早点发生
senses.definition: very keen for something to begin or arrive
senses.definitionCN: 非常渴望某事开始或到来
senses.example: We were impatient to see the results.
senses.exampleCN: 我们急切地想看到结果。
senses.why: The same lack of endurance can point forward: not annoyance at the delay, but hunger for the end of it.
senses.whyCN: 同一份「忍不住」也可以朝前指：不是恼火于耽误，而是渴望它结束。

senses.title: Showing a restless manner
senses.titleCN: 急躁的：举止上显得坐不住
senses.definition: showing by movement or tone that one cannot wait
senses.definitionCN: 通过动作或语气显出等不下去
senses.example: He gave an impatient wave and walked away.
senses.exampleCN: 他不耐烦地挥了下手就走开了。
senses.why: Because the word names a failure of endurance, the body shows it first: the hand, the foot, the tone.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词命名的是「忍功的失守」，最先泄底的是身体：手、脚和语气。

intro.en: Impatient joins Latin in-, not, to patients, bearing or suffering, from pati.
intro.cn: impatient 由拉丁语 in-「不」加 patiens「能承受的」组成，源自动词 pati。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer or to put up with something.
items.cn: pati 意为「忍受、承受」。

items.en: Patiens was the participle, the one who bears a burden.
items.cn: patiens 是分词，指「正在承受的人」。

items.en: Impatiens denied that bearing power: the one who cannot hold on.
items.cn: impatiens 否定这份承受力：承受不住的人。

items.en: French impatient kept both the annoyance and the eagerness.
items.cn: 法语 impatient 同时保留了烦躁与急切两种意思。

items.en: English uses the word for waiting, and also for eager wanting.
items.cn: 英语用它指等待时的烦躁，也指渴望。

note.en: The look-alike group centres on the pati root with and without negation; the near-meaning group contrasts impatience with eagerness and irritability.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 pati 词根的肯定与否定形式；近义组把「不耐烦」与「急切」「易怒」区分开。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to wait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不耐烦」。

entries.definition: Able to wait calmly; also a person under medical care.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有耐心的」；同形名词指「病人」。

entries.definition: The ability to bear a long wait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「耐心」，与 impatient 同根。

entries.definition: Very keen and ready, without the annoyance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「渴望的」，不含烦躁。

entries.definition: Unable to stay still, often from boredom.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坐立不安的」。

entries.definition: Easily annoyed, a wider temper word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易怒的」，脾气层面更广。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pati root, the tapping fingers and the pair patience and patient.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 pati 词根、敲桌的手指以及 patience 与 patient 这一对词。

normal.en: Im- is not, patient is bearing: impatient means you cannot bear the wait.
normal.cn: im- 是「不」，patient 是「能承受」：impatient 就是受不住这份等。

normal.en: Patient holds two lives: the calm waiter and the sick person, both from Latin pati, to suffer.
normal.cn: patient 有两条命：沉得住气的人与生病的人，都出自拉丁语 pati「忍受」。

normal.en: Drop the im- and the word turns into praise.
normal.cn: 去掉 im-，这个词立刻变成褒义。

normal.en: Impatient with, not impatient of: the preposition is with.
normal.cn: 搭配是 impatient with，不用 of。

normal.en: Impatiens is also the busy touch-me-not flower that bursts when touched.
normal.cn: Impatiens 也是一种「凤仙花」，一碰就弹开，正好对应这个「等不住」。

abstract.en: Impatience is patience measured against a clock.
abstract.cn: 不耐烦，就是拿耐心去对着时钟量。

abstract.en: Waiting is not empty time; it is the part of the task that cannot be hurried.
abstract.cn: 等待不是空白时间，而是任务里催不快的那一部分。

abstract.en: Eagerness pulls forward; impatience pushes away.
abstract.cn: 急切把东西往前拉，不耐烦把它推开。

examples.en: She is patient with slow learners but impatient with excuses.
examples.cn: 她对学得慢的人有耐心，对借口却不耐烦。

examples.en: The driver gave an impatient honk.
examples.cn: 司机不耐烦地按了一下喇叭。

examples.en: The reader became impatient after three long pages.
examples.cn: 读了三页长文之后，读者变得不耐烦了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一姆陪什特」——连陪一会儿都不肯，是典型的不耐烦。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ patiens（忍受的，来自 pati 忍受）→ impatiens；同族词有 patience、patient、impatience、impatiently。

sensesIntro.en: Impatient denies the power to bear a wait, and the three senses split into annoyance, eagerness and visible restlessness.
sensesIntro.cn: impatient 否定的是「承受等待」的能力，三个义项分别落在烦躁、急切与举止上的坐不住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers tapping a table while the clock crawls.
core.cn: 核心意象：时钟慢吞吞地走，手指在桌上敲。

branches.en: WAIT LINE: the wait itself becomes unbearable.
branches.cn: 等待线：等待本身变得难以忍受。

branches.en: DESIRE LINE: the wanting runs ahead of events.
branches.cn: 渴望线：想要跑在事情前面。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the feeling leaks into gestures.
branches.cn: 身体线：情绪从动作里漏出来。

branches.en: CONTRAST: patience is the same root with a yes.
branches.cn: 对照线：patience 是同一词根的肯定版。

branches.en: PAIR LINE: patient also means a sick person, still bearing.
branches.cn: 同形线：patient 还指病人，仍在承受。

intro.en: A negative prefix on the participle for bearing, next to the noun and adjective it denies.
intro.cn: 否定前缀加在「承受」的分词上，旁边就是它所否定的名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati gave patiens, bearing; with in- it became impatiens, unable to bear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati 生出 patiens「能忍的」，加 in- 成为 impatiens「忍不住的」。

items.example: It reverses the bearing named by the stem.
items.exampleCN: 它把词干所指的「忍」反转。

items.example: The stem of patience and patient.
items.exampleCN: patience 与 patient 的词根。

items.example: It forms the adjective from a verb.

definition_en: to put a plan or decision into action, or a tool used for a job
core_image: 图纸摊在桌上，第二天就有人照着它把东西做出来
scene: 方案讨论完了，接下来就该动手。The school will implement the new timetable next term.
sceneCN: 这里 implement 是「实施」（第 1 个义项：把计划付诸行动）；句意是学校下学期将实施新的课表。

pos.zh: 动词：实施；执行；落实
名词：工具；器具；农具

derivatives.zh: 由 implement 加 -ation 构成，义为「实施、落实」
义为「起工具作用的、有帮助的」

senses.title: To put a plan into effect
senses.definition: to carry out a plan or decision in practice
senses.definitionCN: 把计划或决定在现实中执行
senses.example: The school will implement the new timetable next term.
senses.exampleCN: 学校下学期将实施新的课表。
senses.why: Latin implere means to fill up, and the noun implementum was something that filled a need; the modern verb keeps that sense of making a plan real.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 implere 意为「填满」，名词 implementum 指「用来补足所需的东西」；现代动词保留的就是「让计划落地」的意思。

senses.title: To perform a set duty
senses.definition: to carry out a duty or an order that has been set
senses.definitionCN: 把规定好的职责或命令执行完
senses.example: The manager had to implement the committee's decision.
senses.exampleCN: 经理必须执行委员会的决定。
senses.why: Carrying out a decision is treated as a duty, so the verb stretches from plans to orders.
senses.whyCN: 执行决定被看作一种职责，于是这个动词从计划一路伸到命令。

senses.title: In computing, to make a design work
senses.titleCN: 实现：在计算机里让设计跑起来
senses.definition: to build a working version of a system or design
senses.definitionCN: 把某个系统或设计建成可运行的版本
senses.example: The team implemented the search function in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在一周内实现了搜索功能。
senses.why: Software turned the noun tool into a verb again: to implement is to build the thing that makes the design work.
senses.whyCN: 软件把「工具」这个名词再次用作动词：implement 就是造出让设计能跑起来的那个东西。

senses.title: A tool for work
senses.definition: a tool or device used to do a task
senses.definitionCN: 用来完成任务的工具或器械
senses.example: The garden implements were kept behind the shed.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺工具放在小屋后面。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, and it explains the verb: a tool is what makes a task possible at all.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，也解释了动词：工具正是让一件事得以办成的东西。

senses.title: A means to a purpose
senses.definition: anything used as a means to reach an aim
senses.definitionCN: 为达成目标而被使用的事物
senses.example: Language is the chief implement of thought.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是思想最主要的工具。
senses.why: From hammers to words is a short jump: anything that fills a need can be called an implement.
senses.whyCN: 从锤子跳到词语只差一步：凡是能补足所需的东西，都可以叫 implement。

intro.en: Implement comes from Latin implementum, a filling up, from implere, to fill in.
intro.cn: implement 来自拉丁语 implementum「填满之物」，源于 implere「填满」。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, plain in words like plenty.
items.cn: plere 意为「填满」，在 plenty 一类词里还看得见。

items.en: Implere meant to fill up, to complete something.
items.cn: implere 意为「填满、完成某事」。

items.en: Implementum was whatever filled a need, first a tool.
items.cn: implementum 指「补足所需之物」，最初指工具。

items.en: English kept the noun for tools and farm gear.
items.cn: 英语保留名词义，指工具与农具。

items.en: The verb implement, to carry out, grew in official use.
items.cn: 动词「实施」的用法在公文语言里壮大起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the plere root; the near-meaning group separates executing a plan from the tool that does it.
note.cn: 形近组共用 plere 词根；近义组区分「执行计划」与「执行所用工具」。

entries.definition: The act of carrying a plan out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「实施、落实」。

entries.definition: Tools or pieces of equipment for work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，义为「工具、器具」。

entries.definition: Something added to fill a gap; shares Latin plere, to fill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充物」，与 implement 共用拉丁语 plere「填满」，前缀不同。

entries.definition: The everyday phrasal verb for putting a plan into practice.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「执行」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To make people obey a rule or law.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强制执行」，强调使之被遵守。

entries.definition: A simple object held in the hand to do work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工具」，指手上的器具。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the plere root, the drawing becomes a thing image and the policy collocation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 plere 词根、图纸变成实物的意象与政策搭配。

normal.en: Implement shares plere, to fill, with supply and complete.
normal.cn: implement 与 supply、complete 共用 plere「填满」。

normal.en: A tool fills a need, and carrying out a plan fills a gap between plan and world.
normal.cn: 工具补足需求，落实计划则补上计划与现实之间的缺口。

normal.en: Implement a policy is the phrase of every ministry report.
normal.cn: implement a policy 是各类公文里的常客。

normal.en: Implementation is the noun that judges a plan: was it done?
normal.cn: implementation 这个名词就是对计划的拷问：到底做了没有？

normal.en: Farm implements are the oldest implements of all.
normal.cn: farm implements 是最古老的工具。

abstract.en: A plan that is never implemented is only an opinion.
abstract.cn: 从未被实施的计划，只是一种意见。

abstract.en: The tool and the act share one word because both close a gap.
abstract.cn: 工具与行动共用一词，因为二者都在补缺口。

abstract.en: Between decision and result lies the whole weight of implementation.
abstract.cn: 决定与结果之间，压着「落实」的全部重量。

examples.en: The company will implement the new safety rules in June.
examples.cn: 公司将在六月实施新的安全规定。

examples.en: Old farm implements hang on the barn wall.
examples.cn: 谷仓墙上挂着旧农具。

examples.en: A good idea needs someone to implement it.
examples.cn: 好想法需要一个把它落实的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬不起来？」——计划老是硬不起来落地，就急着找人把它实施下去。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ plere（填满）+ -mentum（名词后缀）→ implementum「补足所需之物」；同族词有 implementation、implementer、supplement、complete。

sensesIntro.en: Implement covers both the thing that fills a gap and the act of filling it, so tools and actions share one word.
sensesIntro.cn: implement 同时覆盖「补缺口的东西」与「补缺口的动作」，因此工具与行动共用一词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawing on paper becoming an object in a workshop.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸上的图纸，在车间里变成实物。

branches.en: PLAN LINE: the decision reaches the ground.
branches.cn: 计划线：决定落到了地面。

branches.en: DUTY LINE: someone is ordered to act.
branches.cn: 职责线：有人被要求去做。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: a design becomes working code.
branches.cn: 机器线：设计变成能跑的代码。

branches.en: TOOL LINE: the noun keeps the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 工具线：名词保留了最古老的义项。

branches.en: CONTRAST: the tool and the act both fill a gap.
branches.cn: 对照线：工具与动作都在补缺口。

intro.en: A prefix of completion on the root for filling, with the family that grew around it.
intro.cn: 表「完成」的前缀加「填满」词根，以及围绕它长出的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin implere, to fill up, gave implementum, a thing that fills a need.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 implere「填满」生出 implementum「补足所需之物」。

items.example: It strengthens the root toward completion.
The stem of complete and supply.
items.exampleCN: complete 与 supply 的词根。

items.example: It turns a verb into a noun.

definition_en: a meaning suggested but not stated, or a possible effect that follows from something
core_image: 一句话说了半句，后半句留在听者心里自己长出来
scene: 他停了一下没说完，屋里人都在琢磨后半句。The implication was that the plan would cost too much.
sceneCN: 这里 implication 是「暗示、言外之意」（第 1 个义项：未明说的含义）；句意是言下之意是这个计划太费钱。

pos.zh: 名词：含义；暗示；（可能的）影响；牵连

derivatives.zh: 由 im- + plicare 构成，义为「暗示、意味着」

senses.title: Something suggested but not said
senses.definition: a meaning that is suggested rather than stated
senses.definitionCN: 没有直接说出、但可被理解的意思
senses.example: The implication was that the plan would cost too much.
senses.exampleCN: 言下之意是这个计划太费钱。
senses.why: Latin implicare means to fold in, and an implication is exactly a meaning folded into the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「折入」，implication 正是「折进句子里的那层意思」。

senses.title: A likely result or consequence
senses.titleCN: 影响：可能随之而来的结果
senses.definition: a possible effect that follows from an action or finding
senses.definitionCN: 由某个行动或发现可能带来的结果
senses.example: The findings have serious implications for public health.
senses.exampleCN: 这些发现对公共卫生有重大影响。
senses.why: From the folded meaning comes the folded future: whatever a finding contains will unfold as an effect.
senses.whyCN: 从折起的意思生出折起的未来：发现里含着的东西，总会作为后果摊开。

senses.title: The act of involving someone
senses.definition: the fact of being involved in something, often a crime
senses.definitionCN: 被卷入某事，常指卷入罪案
senses.example: His implication in the theft shocked his colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 他被牵连进这起盗窃案，让同事们震惊。
senses.why: A person can be folded into an event as well as a meaning, and English keeps the same noun for it.
senses.whyCN: 人也能被折进一桩事件里，正如一句含义被折进句子里，英语用同一个名词说这两件事。

senses.title: A close logical link
senses.titleCN: 蕴含：逻辑上的紧密关联
senses.definition: in logic, a relation in which one statement follows from another
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑上，一个命题可由另一命题推出
senses.example: The argument rests on an implication between two statements.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证依赖两个陈述之间的蕴含关系。
senses.why: In logic the fold is exact: one statement contains another without stating it.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑里这道折叠是精确的：一个命题包含另一个，却没有把它说出来。

intro.en: Implication comes from Latin implicare, to fold in, from in-, in, and plicare, to fold.
intro.cn: implication 来自拉丁语 implicare「折入」，由 in-「进入」与 plicare「折叠」组成。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, as one folds cloth.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，像叠布那样。

items.en: Implicare meant to fold something into something else.
items.cn: implicare 意为「把某物折进另一物中」。

items.en: Implicatio named the folding, and later a tangled involvement.
items.cn: implicatio 指「折叠」，后来又指纠缠不清的牵涉。

items.en: French implication carried both the logical and the legal senses.
items.cn: 法语 implication 同时包含逻辑与法律两种含义。

items.en: English uses implication for hidden meaning and for consequences.
items.cn: 英语用 implication 指隐含的意思和随之而来的后果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the plicare fold; the near-meaning group separates a hinted meaning from a plain one.
note.cn: 形近组共用 plicare「折叠」；近义组区分「暗示之意」与「明说之意」。

entries.definition: To suggest something without saying it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「暗示」，是 implication 的动词形式。

entries.definition: Understood but not expressed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「隐含的、不言明的」。

entries.definition: Stated clearly and directly, the reverse of implicit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明确的」，是 implicit 的反面。

entries.definition: A slight indirect suggestion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暗示」，程度最轻。

entries.definition: A result that follows from something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果」，偏向结果。

entries.definition: The importance or meaning of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「意义、重要性」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fold-in root, the unfinished sentence and the research-report collocation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「折入」词根、没说完的句子与研究报道搭配。

normal.en: Plicare is to fold: an implication is a meaning folded inside the sentence.
normal.cn: plicare 是「折叠」：implication 就是折进句子里的意思。

normal.en: Implicit is the adjective, implication is the noun, imply is the verb.
normal.cn: implicit 是形容词，implication 是名词，imply 是动词。

normal.en: By implication is a fixed phrase meaning without saying so.
normal.cn: by implication 是固定短语，意为「言下之意」。

normal.en: Research papers now end with a section on implications.
normal.cn: 现在的研究论文末尾总有一节讲 implications。

normal.en: Explicit is the same fold opened out in the light.
normal.cn: explicit 就是同一折叠在光下摊开。

abstract.en: Some messages are heavier because they were never said aloud.
abstract.cn: 有些话没说出口，反而更重。

abstract.en: An implication is a door the speaker leaves open for the listener to close.
abstract.cn: implication 是说话人留下的门，由听者自己关上。

abstract.en: Effects travel further than causes, which is why implications outlive plans.
abstract.cn: 影响比原因走得更远，所以言外之意比计划活得久。

examples.en: By implication, the older workers were being pushed out.
examples.cn: 言下之意是年纪大的工人正在被挤走。

examples.en: The report has implications for every school in the country.
examples.cn: 这份报告对全国每所学校都有影响。

examples.en: She resented the implication that she had lied.
examples.cn: 她讨厌那层意思，仿佛她撒了谎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木里凯森」——木头里面藏着森林，未明说的含义也一样藏在句子里。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ plicare（折叠）+ -ation（名词后缀）→ implicatio；同族词有 imply、implicit、implicate、explicit、complicate。

sensesIntro.en: Implication begins as a fold inside a word, then spreads to consequences, to persons involved and to logic.
sensesIntro.cn: implication 起初是折在词句里的那一层，随后延伸到后果、被卷入的人与逻辑关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-finished sentence growing its second half in the listener.
core.cn: 核心意象：半句话在听者心里自己长出下半句。

branches.en: MEANING LINE: the sentence carries more than it says.
branches.cn: 含义线：句子承载的比它说出的多。

branches.en: EFFECT LINE: findings reach into the future.
branches.cn: 影响线：发现伸进未来。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: someone is folded into the case.
branches.cn: 人物线：有人被卷进案子里。

branches.en: LOGIC LINE: one statement folds into another.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：一个命题折进另一个命题。

branches.en: CONTRAST: hint is light, implication can be an accusation.
branches.cn: 对照线：hint 轻，implication 可能是一记指控。

intro.en: A prefix of entry on the Latin root for folding, with the noun ending and the open and closed cousins.
intro.cn: 表「进入」的前缀加「折叠」词根，加上名词词尾，以及「折入」与「摊开」两个表亲。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare, to fold, gave implicare and implicatio, and English built implication on them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plicare「折叠」生出 implicare 与 implicatio，英语在其上造出 implication。

items.example: The stem of complicated and explicit.
items.exampleCN: complicated 与 explicit 的词根。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun.

definition_zh: 进口；输入；进口商品；含义
definition_en: to bring goods in from another country, or goods brought in from abroad
core_image: 货轮靠岸，箱子上印着外国港口的名
scene: 港口每天都有装满货的集装箱卸下。Japan imports most of its oil from abroad.
sceneCN: 这里 import 是「进口」（动词，第 1 个义项：从国外输入货物）；句意是日本的石油大部分靠进口。

pos.zh: 动词：进口；输入；引进
名词：进口；进口商品；含义

derivatives.zh: 由 import 加 -ation 构成，义为「进口、输入」
同源，义为「重要的」，本义为「带来意义的」

senses.title: To bring goods in from abroad
senses.definition: to bring goods into a country from another one
senses.definitionCN: 把货物从另一国运进本国
senses.example: Japan imports most of its oil from abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 日本的石油大部分靠进口。
senses.why: Latin importare is in-, into, plus portare, to carry: to carry in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 importare 是 in-「进入」加 portare「搬运」：搬进来。

senses.title: Goods brought in from abroad
senses.titleCN: 进口商品：从国外运来的货
senses.definition: the goods or services bought in from another country
senses.definitionCN: 从另一国买进来的货物或服务
senses.example: Cheap imports have changed the market.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的进口货改变了市场。
senses.why: The noun simply names the things that the verb brought in.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是把动词搬进来的那些东西命名出来。

senses.title: To bring in ideas or values
senses.titleCN: 引进：把观念、做法带进来
senses.definition: to introduce something abstract from outside
senses.definitionCN: 从外部引入抽象的东西
senses.example: The poets imported new forms from Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人们从欧洲引进了新的形式。
senses.why: Ideas travel in the same ships as goods, so the verb needs no new word for them.
senses.whyCN: 观念与货物搭乘同一批船，所以这个动词不必另造新词。

senses.title: To mean or to matter
senses.definition: to carry a meaning, or the meaning and weight something has
senses.definitionCN: 带有某种意思；某事所含的意思与分量
senses.example: The word "home" imports a sense of safety.
senses.exampleCN: 「家」这个词带有安全的意思。
senses.why: A word can also carry something in: weight, sense, a whole feeling.
senses.whyCN: 一个词也能把东西带进来：分量、意义、一整套感受。

senses.title: In computing, to bring data in
senses.definition: to bring data into a program from another file
senses.definitionCN: 从另一个文件把数据载入程序
senses.example: You can import the list from a spreadsheet.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以从表格里导入这份名单。
senses.why: Software copies the old image: files are carried into a program as crates are carried into a port.
senses.whyCN: 软件沿用的是老画面：文件被搬进程序，正如木箱被搬进港口。

intro.en: Import is Latin in-, into, plus portare, to carry, so it means to carry in.
intro.cn: import 由拉丁语 in-「进入」加 portare「搬运」组成，意为「搬进来」。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, the source of port and transport.
items.cn: portare 意为「搬运」，是 port 与 transport 的来源。

items.en: Importare meant to bring a thing in.
items.cn: importare 意为「把东西带进来」。

items.en: The participle also took up the sense of carrying meaning.
items.cn: 这个分词也承担了「带有意义」的含义。

items.en: French importer supplied the commercial sense to English.
items.cn: 法语 importer 把商业义带进英语。

items.en: Modern use ranges from ships to spreadsheets.
items.cn: 现代用法从货轮一直覆盖到电子表格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares portare, to carry; the near-meaning group separates bringing in, sending out and buying in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 portare「搬运」；近义组区分「运入」「运出」与「买入」。

entries.definition: To send goods out to another country.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出口」，方向与 import 相反。

entries.definition: A person or firm that brings goods in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进口商」。

entries.definition: Light enough to be carried.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「便携的」，同根。

entries.definition: The plain phrasal verb for the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「引入」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To bring something in for the first time, often an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引进」，多用于观念。

entries.definition: To bring goods by sea or carrier.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「运进」，强调运输。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the portare root, the dock image and the computing sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 portare 词根、码头意象与计算机用法。

normal.en: Port is to carry, so import is to carry in and export is to carry out.
normal.cn: port 是「搬运」，所以 import 是搬进来，export 是搬出去。

normal.en: The noun is IMport, the verb is imPORT: stress marks the difference.
normal.cn: 名词读 IMport，动词读 imPORT，重音区分词性。

normal.en: Import duties are the taxes a country puts at the door.
normal.cn: import duties 是国家在门口收的税。

normal.en: Important descends from import: what carries weight.
normal.cn: important 出自 import：能带分量的东西。

normal.en: Computing imports files the way a port imports crates.
normal.cn: 计算机导入文件，就像港口进口木箱。

abstract.en: To import is to admit that something better exists elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 进口，就是承认别处有更好的东西。

abstract.en: Words also cross borders, and they pay no duty.
abstract.cn: 词语也在过境，而且不交关税。

abstract.en: Meaning is what a sentence carries in under its own name.
abstract.cn: 意义是句子以自己名义带进来的东西。

examples.en: The country imports more food than it grows.
examples.cn: 这个国家进口的粮食比种出来的还多。

examples.en: Imports rose sharply last year.
examples.cn: 去年进口额大幅上升。

examples.en: These rules were imported from abroad and never fit here.
examples.cn: 这些规矩是从国外搬来的，从没在这儿合适过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一母炮特」——整船炮弹特地从海外运进来，这就是进口。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ portare（搬运）→ importare；同族词有 export、transport、portable、importer、important。

sensesIntro.en: Import carries something in, and what is carried shifts from goods to ideas, then to meaning and to data.
sensesIntro.cn: import 的核心是「往里搬」，被搬的东西从货物挪到观念，再挪到含义与数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ship unloads crates marked with a foreign port.
core.cn: 核心意象：货轮卸下印着外国港口的木箱。

branches.en: GOODS LINE: the trade sense, the everyday one.
branches.cn: 货物线：最日常的贸易义。

branches.en: PRODUCT LINE: the noun names what arrived.
branches.cn: 产品线：名词指已经运到的东西。

branches.en: IDEA LINE: forms and customs travel too.
branches.cn: 观念线：形式与习俗也会迁移。

branches.en: MEANING LINE: weight and sense are carried in words.
branches.cn: 含义线：分量与意思被词携带。

branches.en: DATA LINE: files enter programs by the same verb.
branches.cn: 数据线：文件用同一个动词进入程序。

intro.en: A prefix of direction on the root for carrying, with the whole port- family around it.
intro.cn: 方向前缀加「搬运」词根，周围是整个 port- 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare, to carry, produced importare and exportare, the two directions of trade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 portare「搬运」生出 importare 与 exportare，即贸易的两个方向。

items.example: The stem of transport and portable.
items.exampleCN: transport 与 portable 的词根。

definition_en: the quality of being important, or the fact of mattering a great deal
core_image: 桌上堆满文件，只有一份被放到最上面
scene: 开会材料一大堆，最重要的一份被放在最上面。She stressed the importance of sleep for young children.
sceneCN: 这里 importance 是「重要性」（第 1 个义项：重要、分量重）；句意是她强调幼儿睡眠的重要性。

pos.zh: 名词：重要性；重要；重大

derivatives.zh: 义为「重要的」，是 importance 的形容词
义为「重要地」，多用于 most importantly 等短语
加 un- 表否定，义为「不重要的」

senses.title: The state of mattering
senses.titleCN: 重要性：分量重、值得重视
senses.definition: the quality of having great value or effect
senses.definitionCN: 具有重大价值或影响的性质
senses.example: She stressed the importance of sleep for young children.
senses.exampleCN: 她强调幼儿睡眠的重要性。
senses.why: Importance names the weight a thing carries, and portare, to carry, is exactly that image of weight.
senses.whyCN: importance 指一件事所带的分量，而 portare「搬运」正是这种「带分量」的意象。

senses.title: High rank or standing
senses.definition: the state of having a high position
senses.definitionCN: 位置高、地位显要
senses.example: He spoke with the air of a man of importance.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话带着一副要人的气派。
senses.why: A person who carries weight in public life is described by the same noun, because social rank is measured like weight.
senses.whyCN: 在公众生活中有分量的人也用这个词，因为社会地位正像分量一样被衡量。

senses.title: Weight given to something
senses.definition: the weight that someone gives to a matter
senses.definitionCN: 某人给某件事的分量
senses.example: The school attaches great importance to art.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校非常重视艺术。
senses.why: If importance is weight, then attaching importance is literally loading weight onto a matter, which is why the verb attach fits.
senses.whyCN: 既然 importance 是分量，attach importance 就等于往一件事上加载分量，所以动词用 attach 才合适。

senses.title: Seriousness of a matter
senses.definition: the seriousness of an event or problem
senses.definitionCN: 事件或问题不容轻视的程度
senses.example: The importance of the leak only became clear later.
senses.exampleCN: 那次泄漏的严重性后来才显现出来。
senses.why: A heavy thing cannot be brushed aside, so a serious matter is said to have importance, the same weight metaphor turned to danger.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的东西挥之不去，所以严重的事也被说成有 importance，同一个「分量」比喻转向了危险的一面。

intro.en: Importance is built on import, which is Latin in- plus portare, to carry: weight carried in.
intro.cn: importance 由 import 派生，即拉丁语 in- 加 portare「搬运」：带进来的分量。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, the source of transport.
items.cn: portare 意为「搬运」，是 transport 的来源。

items.en: Importare meant to bring in, and later to matter.
items.cn: importare 意为「带进来」，后来又引申为「有分量」。

items.en: Importantia named the quality of carrying weight.
items.cn: importantia 指「有分量」这一性质。

items.en: French importance fixed the modern shape.
items.cn: 法语 importance 固定了现代拼写。

items.en: English uses importance for anything that matters.
items.cn: 英语用 importance 指一切有分量的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group is the import family; the near-meaning group separates importance from value and significance.
note.cn: 形近组是 import 词族；近义组区分「重要性」「价值」与「意义」。

entries.definition: Mattering a great deal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「重要的」。

entries.definition: Used to stress a point, as in most importantly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，用于强调，如 most importantly。

entries.definition: To bring goods in, or to carry meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「进口」，同源。

entries.definition: Importance that comes from meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「意义」，重在含义。

entries.definition: Worth measured by usefulness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「价值」，重在看用处。

entries.definition: The influence a point carries.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分量」，多指话语的影响力。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the portare root, the top file on the pile and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 portare 词根、最上面那份文件以及固定搭配。

normal.en: Importance is from import, to carry in: what has importance is what carries weight.
normal.cn: importance 出自 import「搬进来」：有重要性的东西就是带分量的东西。

normal.en: Attach importance to is the standard phrase for treating something as weighty.
normal.cn: attach importance to 是「重视某事」的标准说法。

normal.en: Of great importance is a formal way to say very important.
normal.cn: of great importance 是 very important 的正式说法。

normal.en: Important is countable as an adjective, importance is not a mass word.
normal.cn: important 可以按形容词用，importance 是不可数名词。

normal.en: Most importantly comes first when listing the last and greatest point.
normal.cn: 列举到最后也最重要的一点时，先说 most importantly。

abstract.en: Importance is a judgement, so it always has someone behind it.
abstract.cn: 重要性是一种判断，背后总有判断的人。

abstract.en: What matters at noon rarely matters at midnight.
abstract.cn: 正午重要的事，午夜几乎都不重要。

abstract.en: Giving something importance is the first active thing a person can do.
abstract.cn: 给某件事以重视，是一个人最先能做的主动行为。

examples.en: Few people understood the importance of the document then.
examples.cn: 当时很少人明白那份文件的重大意义。

examples.en: The report stresses the importance of clean water.
examples.cn: 报告强调了清洁用水的重要性。

examples.en: Do not attach too much importance to one bad week.
examples.cn: 别把糟糕的一周看得太重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬跑疼死」——活再疼也要硬跑，说明这事重要到不能停。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ portare（搬运）+ -antia（名词后缀）→ importantia；同族词有 import、important、importantly。

sensesIntro.en: Importance measures how much weight a thing carries, whether by value, rank, emphasis or seriousness.
sensesIntro.cn: importance 衡量一件事的分量，这份分量可以来自价值、地位、被重视的程度或严重性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pile of files with one placed on top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一摞文件，其中一份被放到最上面。

branches.en: VALUE LINE: the thing has an effect worth caring about.
branches.cn: 价值线：这件事的作用值得在意。

branches.en: RANK LINE: position makes a person important.
branches.cn: 地位线：位置让人显要。

branches.en: EMPHASIS LINE: the weight is given by others.
branches.cn: 重视线：分量是别人给的。

branches.en: SERIOUS LINE: the matter cannot be waved away.
branches.cn: 严重线：这件事不能一挥手带过。

branches.en: CONTRAST: importance is not the same as fame.
branches.cn: 对照线：重要性不等于名气。

intro.en: A prefix of direction, the root for carrying, and the noun ending for a quality.
intro.cn: 方向前缀、表「搬运」的词根，以及表示性质的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin importare, to bring in, gave importantia, the quality of carrying weight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 importare「带进来」生出 importantia，即「有分量」这一性质。

items.example: It points to what is carried in.
items.exampleCN: 它指向被带进来的东西。

items.example: The stem of transport and portable.
items.exampleCN: transport 与 portable 的词根。

items.example: It makes a noun of quality.

definition_zh: 重要的；重大的；有影响的
definition_en: having a great effect or value, and therefore worth attention
core_image: 日程本上，那一栏被圈了两圈
scene: 日程本上，只有那一栏被圈了两圈。It is important to check the figures twice.
sceneCN: 这里 important 是「重要的」（第 1 个义项：影响或价值大，值得重视）；句意是把数字核对两遍很重要。

pos.zh: 形容词：重要的；重大的；有影响的

derivatives.zh: 义为「重要地」，常用于 most importantly

senses.title: Having great value or effect
senses.definition: having a great effect or value
senses.definitionCN: 作用大、值得重视
senses.example: It is important to check the figures twice.
senses.exampleCN: 把数字核对两遍很重要。
senses.why: The word judges how much weight a thing carries, so anything with real effect on a result is called important.
senses.whyCN: 这个词判断一件事带多少分量，所以凡对结果有真实影响的事都叫 important。

senses.title: Holding high rank
senses.definition: having a high position in an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 在组织里位置很高
senses.example: Several important officials attended the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 几位要员出席了典礼。
senses.why: Rank is read as weight too: a person who carries weight in an institution is an important person.
senses.whyCN: 地位同样被读作分量：在一个机构里说话有分量的人就是 an important person。

senses.title: Deserving attention now
senses.definition: needing attention before other matters
senses.definitionCN: 需要先于其他事处理
senses.example: There is an important message for you at the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 前台有给你的紧要消息。
senses.why: A heavy object demands to be handled first, so urgent matters borrow the same word.
senses.whyCN: 重物必须先搬，所以紧急的事也借用了这个词。

senses.title: Carrying a strong point
senses.definition: making a strong or valuable point
senses.definitionCN: 提出有力或有价值的观点
senses.example: She made an important point about the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 她就预算提了一个有分量的意见。
senses.why: A remark that lands with force is said to carry weight, and important is the adjective for that weight.
senses.whyCN: 有冲击力的话被说成「有分量」，important 就是形容这份分量的形容词。

intro.en: Important is the adjective of import: Latin in- plus portare, carrying weight into a matter.
intro.cn: important 是 import 的形容词：拉丁语 in- 加 portare，即把分量带进一件事里。

items.en: Portare, to carry, is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: portare「搬运」是整族词的底子。

items.en: Importare meant to bring in, and came to mean to matter.
items.cn: importare 意为「带进来」，后来变成「有分量」。

items.en: French important fixed the adjective form.
items.cn: 法语 important 固定了形容词形式。

items.en: English important covers value, rank and urgency.
items.cn: 英语的 important 覆盖价值、地位与紧迫。

items.en: It is a workhorse word in school and office alike.
items.cn: 在学校和办公室里都是高频主力词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the import family; the near-meaning group ranks key, significant and vital.
note.cn: 形近组是 import 词族；近义组比较「关键的」「有意义的」与「至关重要的」。

entries.definition: The quality of mattering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重要性」。

entries.definition: Used to stress a point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，用于强调。

entries.definition: Of little weight or consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不重要的」。

entries.definition: Important in a way that carries meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「重要的」，含「有意义」意味。

entries.definition: So important that it cannot be left out.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必不可少的」，程度更重。

entries.definition: Decisive for the outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「关键的」，决定成败。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the whole import family, the circled box and the fixed patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借整个 import 词族、被圈起来的那一栏以及固定句式。

normal.en: Important and import look alike because weight is what they share.
normal.cn: important 与 import 长得像，是因为「分量」这个词义一脉相承。

normal.en: It is important to plus a verb is the most common pattern in exams.
normal.cn: It is important to 加动词是考试里最常见的句式。

normal.en: Important for a purpose, important to a person: watch the preposition.
normal.cn: important for 接目的，important to 接人：注意介词。

normal.en: Importance is the noun, importantly the adverb, important the adjective.
normal.cn: importance 名词，importantly 副词，important 形容词。

normal.en: Unimportant is the quiet way to dismiss a detail.
normal.cn: unimportant 是轻轻带过一个细节的说法。

abstract.en: Everything important needs a deadline, or it stays a hope.
abstract.cn: 重要的事都需要一个截止时间，否则只能停在愿望里。

abstract.en: Important is a claim about weight, not about truth.
abstract.cn: important 说的是分量，不是真假。

abstract.en: What is important to one family is invisible to another.
abstract.cn: 对一个家庭重要的事，对另一个家庭可能看不见。

examples.en: It is important to keep the letters in order.
examples.cn: 把这些信件按顺序放好很重要。

examples.en: She plays an important role in the team.
examples.cn: 她在队里担任重要角色。

examples.en: The most important thing is to stay calm.
examples.cn: 最重要的是保持冷静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬破疼特」——硬碰硬地破了也不疼，因为这件事特别重要。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ portare（搬运）+ -ant（形容词后缀）→ important；同族词有 importance、importantly、import、unimportant。

sensesIntro.en: Important judges weight in four ways: value, rank, urgency and the strength of a point.
sensesIntro.cn: important 从四个方面衡量分量：价值、地位、紧迫与观点的力度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one line in a diary circled twice.
core.cn: 核心意象：日程本上被圈了两圈的那一栏。

branches.en: VALUE LINE: the thing has effect worth caring about.
branches.cn: 价值线：这件事的影响值得在意。

branches.en: RANK LINE: the adjective describes persons too.
branches.cn: 地位线：这个词也能形容人。

branches.en: URGENCY LINE: attention is needed now.
branches.cn: 紧迫线：需要现在就处理。

branches.en: ARGUMENT LINE: the weight is in what is said.
branches.cn: 论证线：分量在所说的话里。

branches.en: CONTRAST: important is weaker than essential.
branches.cn: 对照线：important 比 essential 弱。

intro.en: The prefix of entry, the root for carrying and the adjective ending, with its noun.
intro.cn: 进入前缀、搬运词根、形容词词尾，以及对应的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin importare, to bring in, produced importantia and the French adjective important.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 importare「带进来」产生 importantia 与法语形容词 important。

items.example: It points to what is brought in.
items.exampleCN: 它指向被带进来的东西。

items.example: The stem of portable and transport.
items.exampleCN: portable 与 transport 的词根。

definition_en: in a way that matters, or used to introduce a point worth stressing
core_image: 说完一堆细节，最后一句被说得格外慢
scene: 讲完许多细节，他停了一下才补上一句。More importantly, the whole scheme costs far less.
sceneCN: 这里 importantly 用在 more importantly 中，表示「更重要的是」（第 2 个义项：引出强调的要点）。

pos.zh: 副词：重要地；重要的是

derivatives.zh: 加 un-，义为「无关紧要地」

senses.title: In a significant way
senses.definition: in a way that has great effect
senses.definitionCN: 以影响很大的方式
senses.example: The two events were importantly linked.
senses.exampleCN: 这两件事之间存在重要的关联。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the adjective meaning, so it states that something is linked in a way that matters.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留了形容词的含义，说明两件事的关联方式是有分量的。

senses.title: Used to stress a point
senses.titleCN: 重要的是：引出强调的要点
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to mark what matters most
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，标出最要紧的一点
senses.example: More importantly, the plan is cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 更重要的是，这个方案花费很少。
senses.why: Weight can be ranked, so the adverb works as a signpost that says the next point carries more weight.
senses.whyCN: 分量可以排次序，于是这个副词变成路标，告诉读者下一句分量更重。

senses.title: With an air of self-importance
senses.titleCN: 摆架子地：带着要人的神气
senses.definition: in a manner that suggests the speaker matters a great deal
senses.definitionCN: 举止显出说话者很有地位
senses.example: He looked at his watch importantly.
senses.exampleCN: 他意味深长地看了看表。
senses.why: A person who treats himself as weighty shows it in his manner, and the adverb turns that claim into visible behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 把自己当成分量重的人会从举止里露出来，副词就把这种自我评估变成了可见的行为。

intro.en: Importantly is important plus the adverb ending -ly, and important itself comes from Latin importare, to bring in.
intro.cn: importantly 是 important 加副词词尾 -ly，而 important 出自拉丁语 importare「带进来」。

items.en: Importare meant to bring something in, and so to carry weight.
items.cn: importare 意为「带进来」，因而指「有分量」。

items.en: French supplied the adjective important.
items.cn: 法语提供了形容词 important。

items.en: The English suffix -ly turns it into an adverb.
items.cn: 英语词尾 -ly 把它变成副词。

items.en: More importantly became a fixed way to order arguments.
items.cn: more importantly 成为给论点排序的固定说法。

items.en: Most importantly marks the last and greatest point.
items.cn: most importantly 标出最后也是最大的一点。

note.en: The look-alike group is the important family; the near-meaning group gathers ways to rank points.
note.cn: 形近组是 important 词族；近义组收给论点排序的说法。

entries.definition: Mattering a great deal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「重要的」。

entries.definition: The quality of mattering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重要性」。

entries.definition: In a way that does not matter.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无关紧要地」。

entries.definition: In a notable or measurable way, often before numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「显著地」，多修饰数据。

entries.definition: The phrase for the single most important point.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「最重要的是」。

entries.definition: Singling out one case from a group.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「尤其」，用于挑出个案。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the important family, the slow last sentence and the rank-ordering phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 important 词族、放慢的最后一句以及排序短语。

normal.en: Important plus -ly gives importantly, mostly used with more and most.
normal.cn: important 加 -ly 得到 importantly，多数与 more、most 连用。

normal.en: More importantly moves the argument forward a step.
normal.cn: more importantly 把论证往前推一步。

normal.en: Most importantly always comes before the biggest point.
normal.cn: most importantly 总在最大的那一点之前。

normal.en: Do not confuse importantly with importance: one is an adverb, one a noun.
normal.cn: 别把 importantly 和 importance 混用：一个是副词，一个是名词。

normal.en: The rare sense of acting importantly describes a manner, not a value.
normal.cn: 「摆架子」这个罕见义项说的是举止，不是价值。

abstract.en: Ordering ideas is itself a way of judging them.
abstract.cn: 给想法排队，本身就是一种评判。

abstract.en: The word that comes after importantly is always the one the speaker wants kept.
abstract.cn: importantly 后面那一句，永远是说话人希望被记住的。

abstract.en: Some details matter; the adverb tells us which ones the writer thinks do.
abstract.cn: 细节各有轻重，这个副词告诉我们作者认为哪条重。
