examples.en: The house is old and, more importantly, very cold.
examples.cn: 这房子很老，更重要的是，还特别冷。

examples.en: Most importantly, nobody was hurt.
examples.cn: 最重要的是，没有人受伤。

examples.en: Importantly, the two studies used the same method.
examples.cn: 重要的是，两项研究用了同样的方法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木泡腾特利」——泡腾片一丢进去就炸得特别厉害，特别重要。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ portare（搬运）+ -ant（形容词）+ -ly（副词词尾）→ importantly；同族词有 important、importance、import。

sensesIntro.en: Importantly is mostly a signpost for weight, and only rarely a plain adverb of manner.
sensesIntro.cn: importantly 多半是标示分量的路标，反而很少用来直接修饰动作方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last sentence of a list, spoken slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串细节之后的最后一句，被人说得很慢。

branches.en: MANNER LINE: it describes how something acts.
branches.cn: 方式线：描述某事作用的方式。

branches.en: SIGNPOST LINE: the dominant use in writing.
branches.cn: 路标线：书面里最主要的用法。

branches.en: POSE LINE: a rare, slightly mocking sense.
branches.cn: 姿态线：罕见且略带嘲意。

branches.en: CONTRAST: more importantly ranks, significantly measures.
branches.cn: 对照线：more importantly 排序，significantly 量化。

branches.en: CONTRAST: the signpost use far outnumbers the manner use.
branches.cn: 对照线：路标用法远多于修饰举止的用法。

intro.en: The adjective of import plus the English adverb ending, plus a negative cousin.
intro.cn: import 的形容词加英语副词词尾，另有否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin importare, to bring in, led to important, and English added -ly for the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 importare「带进来」引出 important，英语再加 -ly 成副词。

items.example: It marks what is carried in.
items.exampleCN: 它标记被带进来的东西。

items.example: The stem of import and portable.
items.exampleCN: import 与 portable 的词根。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an adverb.

definition_zh: 不可能的；办不到的；难以忍受的
definition_en: not able to happen or to be done
core_image: 一扇门被砖砌死，门牌还挂在那里
scene: 任务发下来，所有人都摇头。It is impossible to finish the report by Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 impossible 是「不可能的」（第 1 个义项：无法发生或做到）；句意是周五前完成报告是不可能的。

pos.zh: 形容词：不可能的；办不到的；难以忍受的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀，义为「可能的」
由 impossible 加 -ity 构成，义为「不可能性」
义为「不可能地」，常作夸张修饰

senses.title: Not able to happen
senses.definition: not able to happen at all
senses.definitionCN: 根本没有发生的可能
senses.example: It is impossible to finish the report by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 周五前完成这份报告是不可能的。
senses.why: The negative prefix im- closes the ability carried by posse, so what cannot happen at all is called impossible.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 im- 关掉了 posse 所带的「能够」，所以根本不会发生的事就叫 impossible。

senses.title: Not able to be done
senses.definition: not able to be done by anyone
senses.definitionCN: 任何人都做不到
senses.example: Climbing that wall without a rope is impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 不用绳子爬那面墙是不可能的。
senses.why: The same denied ability applies to work rather than to events, so a job beyond anyone is impossible to do.
senses.whyCN: 被否定的仍是「能够」，只是针对做事而非事件，所以谁都做不到的活就是 impossible to do。

senses.title: Very hard to deal with
senses.titleCN: 难以相处的：让人受不了
senses.definition: extremely difficult to live or work with
senses.definitionCN: 极难相处或应付
senses.example: He becomes impossible when he is tired.
senses.exampleCN: 他一累就变得难以相处。
senses.why: A door bricked up cannot let anyone through, so a person nobody can get along with is described by the same blocked image.
senses.whyCN: 砌死的门谁也过不去，所以谁也相处不来的人也用这幅被堵住的画面来形容。

senses.title: Hard to believe or accept
senses.titleCN: 让人无法接受的：不可思议
senses.definition: so bad or strange that it cannot be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 坏或怪到无法接受
senses.example: The room was in an impossible state.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里乱得让人无法接受。
senses.why: What cannot be accepted behaves like what cannot be: the mind refuses it as firmly as the body refuses a wall.
senses.whyCN: 无法接受的东西表现得像无法存在的东西：心里拒绝它，像身体撞墙一样坚决。

intro.en: Impossible joins Latin in-, not, to possibilis, able to be done, from posse, to be able.
intro.cn: impossible 由拉丁语 in-「不」加 possibilis「可行的」组成，源于 posse「能够」。

items.en: Posse meant to be able, the root of power as well.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够」，也是 power 的词根。

items.en: Possibilis meant able to be done.
items.cn: possibilis 意为「能够被做到的」。

items.en: Impossibilis simply denied that ability.
items.cn: impossibilis 直接否定这份能力。

items.en: French impossible carried the word into English.
items.cn: 法语 impossible 把它带进英语。

items.en: English uses it for facts, tasks and tempers alike.
items.cn: 英语用它说事实、说任务，也说脾气。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with possible and its prefixes; the near-meaning group ranks unthinkable, unavoidable and impracticable.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 possible 与各前缀；近义组区分「难以想象」「不可避免」与「不可行」。

entries.definition: Able to happen or be done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可能的」，去掉否定前缀。

entries.definition: A thing that could happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可能性」。

entries.definition: A thing that cannot be.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不可能之事」。

entries.definition: So bad or unlikely that nobody would consider it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以想象的」，多含价值判断。

entries.definition: Possible in theory but not workable in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可行的」，理论上可能但做不成。

entries.definition: Leaving no chance of success.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无望的」，语气更情绪化。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the posse root, the bricked-up door and the common patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 posse 词根、砌死的门以及常见句式。

normal.en: Im- is not, possible is able to be done: impossible closes the door.
normal.cn: im- 是「不」，possible 是「做得到」：impossible 把门关上。

normal.en: It is impossible to plus a verb is the pattern to learn first.
normal.cn: It is impossible to 加动词是最该先掌握的句式。

normal.en: Next to impossible is softer: almost, not quite.
normal.cn: next to impossible 语气更软：几乎，而非绝对。

normal.en: Impossibly is often used to exaggerate an adjective: impossibly young.
normal.cn: impossibly 常拿来夸张修饰：impossibly young。

normal.en: Possible and power share the Latin posse, to be able.
normal.cn: possible 与 power 共用拉丁语 posse「能够」。

abstract.en: Impossible is often only a report on what has not been tried yet.
abstract.cn: 「不可能」往往只是对「还没试过」的汇报。

abstract.en: The impossible task is usually the badly defined one.
abstract.cn: 所谓不可能的任务，常常是没定义清楚的任务。

abstract.en: A person called impossible is often just tired.
abstract.cn: 被叫作「难以相处」的人，往往只是累了。

examples.en: It seems impossible that the letter was lost twice.
examples.cn: 那封信丢两次，似乎不可能。

examples.en: Finding the original manuscript was thought impossible.
examples.cn: 找到原稿曾被认为不可能。

examples.en: She was impossible to argue with when she was sure.
examples.cn: 她一旦确信，就没人能跟她争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木泡色抱」——木头泡了色就抱成一团，怎么也拆不开，办不到了。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ possibilis（可行的，来自 posse 能够）→ impossibilis；同族词有 possible、possibility、impossibility、power。

sensesIntro.en: Impossible denies possibility, and then stretches to people and situations that cannot be put up with.
sensesIntro.cn: impossible 否定的是可能性，随后延伸到无法忍受的人与局面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway bricked up, with the number still on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：门被砖砌死了，门牌还挂着。

branches.en: EVENT LINE: the thing cannot come about.
branches.cn: 事件线：这件事根本无法发生。

branches.en: TASK LINE: nobody can finish it.
branches.cn: 任务线：没人能做成。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: the word judges temper.
branches.cn: 人物线：这个词评判脾气。

branches.en: SITUATION LINE: the state cannot be accepted.
branches.cn: 处境线：这种状况无法接受。

branches.en: CONTRAST: next to impossible admits a tiny chance.
branches.cn: 对照线：next to impossible 还留了一点可能。

intro.en: A negating prefix on the adjective for what can be done, with the noun family.
intro.cn: 否定前缀加在「可做到的」形容词上，旁边是名词词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse, to be able, gave possibilis and impossibilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 posse「能够」生出 possibilis 与 impossibilis。

items.example: The stem of possible and potent.
items.exampleCN: possible 与 potent 的词根。

items.example: It makes an adjective of possibility.
items.exampleCN: 它造出表可能性的形容词。

definition_en: to become better, or to make something better
core_image: 一片荒地被翻土、修渠，慢慢长出了收成
scene: 老房子翻修之后，屋里亮了许多。His English improved quickly after a year abroad.
sceneCN: 这里 improve 是「提高、进步」（第 1 个义项：变得更好）；句意是在国外待了一年之后，他的英语提高很快。

pos.zh: 动词：改善；提高；改进；（身体）好转

derivatives.zh: 由 improve 加 -ment 构成，义为「改进、改善」
义为「有教益的、提高人的」
加 un- 表否定，义为「未改善的」

senses.title: To make something better
senses.definition: to make something better in quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 提高某物的质量或状况
senses.example: We need to improve the train service.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要改善列车服务。
senses.why: The French source meant to turn something to profit, so the verb always implies effort put in.
senses.whyCN: 法语词源本指「使之有收益」，所以这个动词总带着「得下功夫」的意思。

senses.title: To become better
senses.definition: to get better without an outside maker
senses.definitionCN: 自身变得更好
senses.example: His English improved quickly after a year abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外待了一年之后，他的英语提高很快。
senses.why: Without an object the verb turns inward and the subject is the one getting better.
senses.whyCN: 不带宾语时，这个动词转向自身，主语就是变好的那一个。

senses.title: To beat a previous standard
senses.definition: to do better than something already done
senses.definitionCN: 做得比已有的更好
senses.example: No one has improved on her record in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年来没人打破过她的纪录。
senses.why: Improve on needs the on: the comparison is with a standard that already exists.
senses.whyCN: improve on 中的 on 不能省：比较对象是已有的标准。

senses.title: To turn land to good use
senses.titleCN: 改良（土地）：让地变得值钱
senses.definition: to raise the value or yield of land
senses.definitionCN: 提高土地的价值或产量
senses.example: The farmers improved the marsh with drains.
senses.exampleCN: 农民修了排水沟把沼泽改成了良田。
senses.why: This is the original sense, where value is added to soil rather than to a service.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的含义，加值对象是土壤，不是服务。

senses.title: To recover in health
senses.definition: to get healthier after an illness
senses.definitionCN: 病后身体转好
senses.example: The old man improved steadily through the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 老人的身体整个夏天都在稳步好转。
senses.why: Health is just another ground that can be brought back to a good state.
senses.whyCN: 健康不过是另一块可以被养回好状态的地。

intro.en: Improve came through Anglo-French emprower, to turn to profit, from Old French prou, profit.
intro.cn: improve 经英法法语 emprower「使之有利可图」而来，源于古法语 prou「利益」。

items.en: Prou meant profit or advantage.
items.cn: prou 意为「利益、好处」。

items.en: Emprower meant to turn land to profit.
items.cn: emprower 意为「把土地经营得有利可图」。

items.en: English wrote it improwen, still mostly about land.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 improwen，仍多指土地。

items.en: The meaning widened from land to anything worth raising.
items.cn: 词义从土地扩展到一切值得提高的事物。

items.en: Improve now covers health, skills and service alike.
items.cn: 如今 improve 覆盖健康、技能与服务。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the prove stem; the near-meaning group separates raising, refining and growing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 prove 词干；近义组区分「提升」「改进」与「变好」。

entries.definition: The act or result of getting better.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改进、改善」。

entries.definition: Made better than before.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「改良过的」。

entries.definition: To show that something is true; spelled near improve but from a different French branch.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证明」，与 improve 拼写相近，但出自法语的另一支。

entries.definition: To increase the quality or value of something, more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提升」，更正式。

entries.definition: To polish by removing faults in small steps.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「精细改进」，强调细微打磨。

entries.definition: The plain spoken phrase for both senses.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「变好」，口语最常用。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the prou profit origin, the drained marsh and the fixed collocation with on.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 prou「利益」词源、排干的沼泽以及 on 的固定搭配。

normal.en: Improve came from profit, not from proving: to improve land was to make it pay.
normal.cn: improve 来自「利润」而不是「证明」：改良土地就是让它产出。

normal.en: Improve on means to do better than; improve just means to make better.
normal.cn: improve on 意为胜于，improve 只表示使之更好。

normal.en: Improvement is countable: a small improvement, several improvements.
normal.cn: improvement 可数：a small improvement，several improvements。

normal.en: Improving books are the ones that improve you.
normal.cn: improving books 指能提升人的书。

normal.en: The verb works without an object when the subject gets better by itself.
normal.cn: 主语自己变好时，这个动词不带宾语。

abstract.en: Improvement is the slowest form of change and the only one that keeps.
abstract.cn: 改善是最慢的变化，也是唯一留得住的那种。

abstract.en: You cannot improve a thing you have never measured.
abstract.cn: 没量过的东西，你没法改进。

abstract.en: To improve on the past you first have to admit it was good.
abstract.cn: 要胜过往昔，先得承认它曾经不错。

examples.en: The weather improved after lunch.
examples.cn: 午后天色好转。

examples.en: Practice is the only way to improve your writing.
examples.cn: 练习是提高写作的唯一办法。

examples.en: The design improves on last year's model in every way.
examples.cn: 这个设计在各方面都胜过去年的型号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木扑入夫」——把一块木头扑进丈夫手里，帮他修房，改善居住。

root: 古法语 prou（利益）+ 英法法语 em- → emprower「使有利可图」→ 中古英语 improwen → improve；同族词有 improvement、improving、unimproved。

sensesIntro.en: Improve began as making land pay and has widened to anything that can be raised, then also to people getting well.
sensesIntro.cn: improve 从「让土地有产出」起步，扩展到一切可以提高的东西，也扩展到人的康复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marsh drained and planted, turning into a field of grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：排干水的沼泽种上庄稼，变成一片麦田。

branches.en: MAKING LINE: an outside hand raises quality.
branches.cn: 施加线：外面的手提高质量。

branches.en: GROWING LINE: the subject rises on its own.
branches.cn: 生长线：主语自己升高。

branches.en: STANDARD LINE: the old record is passed.
branches.cn: 标准线：旧纪录被越过。

branches.en: LAND LINE: the oldest sense, value added to soil.
branches.cn: 土地线：最古老的义项，给土壤加值。

branches.en: HEALTH LINE: the body follows the same path.
branches.cn: 健康线：身体走的是同一条路。

intro.en: A French prefix for making and a French noun for profit, with the noun for the result.
intro.cn: 法语「使成为」前缀加法语「利益」名词，再加表示结果的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is French rather than Latin: em- plus prou, profit, became emprower.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词走的是法语而非拉丁语路线：em- 加 prou「利益」成为 emprower。

items.example: It makes the state named by prou.
items.exampleCN: 它把 prou 所指的状态做出来。

items.example: The source of the modern verb improves.

definition_zh: 改进；改善；提高；改进之处
definition_en: the act of making something better, or a change that makes it better
core_image: 旧机器换上新零件，声音一下子轻了
scene: 换了新零件，机器声音立刻轻了半截。There has been a marked improvement in air quality.
sceneCN: 这里 improvement 是「改善」（第 1 个义项：变好的过程或结果）；句意是空气质量有明显改善。

pos.zh: 名词：改进；改善；提高；改进之处

senses.title: The act of getting better
senses.titleCN: 改善：变好的过程或结果
senses.definition: the process or result of becoming better
senses.definitionCN: 变好的过程或结果
senses.example: There has been a marked improvement in air quality.
senses.exampleCN: 空气质量有明显改善。
senses.why: The noun names the whole event of turning something to better account, the original sense of profit applied to any condition.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指「把某事经营得更有收益」这一整个事件，最初的「获利」义被用到了任何状况上。

senses.title: A change that makes things better
senses.titleCN: 改进之处：具体改了什么
senses.definition: a change made to make something better
senses.definitionCN: 为了让某物更好所做的改动
senses.example: The new model has three small improvements.
senses.exampleCN: 新型号有三处小改进。
senses.why: Once the result can be counted, each separate change that produced it is also called an improvement.
senses.whyCN: 结果一旦可以数出来，促成它的每一处改动也就同样被称作 improvement。

senses.title: Room for further work
senses.definition: the chance to make something better still
senses.definitionCN: 还可以做得更好的空间
senses.example: There is still room for improvement in your essay.
senses.exampleCN: 你的文章还有改进余地。
senses.why: If an improvement adds profit, then room for improvement is the space where more profit could still be made.
senses.whyCN: 既然 improvement 是增加收益，那么 room for improvement 就是还能再赚到的那块空间。

senses.title: Recovery in health
senses.definition: a return to better health
senses.definitionCN: 健康状况转好
senses.example: The doctor noted a slight improvement by Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到到周日时病情已略有好转。
senses.why: The body is treated like land to be brought into better condition, so a patient gaining strength shows an improvement.
senses.whyCN: 身体被当作一块要养好的地来打理，病人恢复元气就表现为 improvement。

intro.en: Improvement joins improve to the French noun ending -ment; improve itself came from Anglo-French emprower, to turn to profit.
intro.cn: improvement 是 improve 加法语名词词尾 -ment；improve 本身来自英法法语 emprower「使之有利可图」。

items.en: Prou meant profit, and emprower meant to turn land to profit.
items.cn: prou 意为「利益」，emprower 意为「把土地经营得有收益」。

items.en: English improwen first described land made productive.
items.cn: 中古英语 improwen 先指把土地经营得高产。

items.en: The noun improvement followed the verb closely.
items.cn: 名词 improvement 紧跟着动词出现。

items.en: The sense widened to skills, services and health.
items.cn: 词义扩展到技能、服务与健康。

items.en: Improvements are now countable, one by one.
items.cn: 如今的 improvement 可数，可以一条条数。

note.en: The look-alike group is the improve family; the near-meaning group separates improvement from progress and reform.
note.cn: 形近组是 improve 词族；近义组区分「改进」「进展」与「改革」。

entries.definition: To make or become better.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改善」。

entries.definition: Made better than before.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「改良的」。

entries.definition: Left as it was.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未改良的」。

entries.definition: Movement forward over time, a wider word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进展」，范围更宽。

entries.definition: A structured change to a system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改革」，多指制度。

entries.definition: A move to a better model or level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「升级」，多指设备。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the improve plus -ment build, the new part image and the fixed prepositions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 improve 加 -ment 的构词、换零件的意象以及固定介词。

normal.en: Improve plus -ment makes the noun improvement, countable in most uses.
normal.cn: improve 加 -ment 成为名词 improvement，多数用法可数。

normal.en: An improvement in a subject, improvements to a thing.
normal.cn: an improvement in 接领域，improvements to 接具体对象。

normal.en: Room for improvement is the polite phrase on every report card.
normal.cn: room for improvement 是每份评语里那句客套话。

normal.en: Home improvement is a whole industry named by this noun.
normal.cn: home improvement 是靠这个名词撑起的整个行业。

normal.en: Unimproved land is land nobody has worked on.
normal.cn: unimproved land 是没人经营过的地。

abstract.en: An improvement is only measurable against a baseline nobody likes to name.
abstract.cn: 改进只能对着一条没人愿提的基线来量。

abstract.en: Small improvements kept up outrun one big change.
abstract.cn: 持续的小改进胜过一次性的大改动。

abstract.en: The best improvement is often the removal of something.
abstract.cn: 最好的改进往往是把某样东西去掉。

examples.en: The team showed clear improvement in the second half.
examples.cn: 球队在下半场有明显进步。

examples.en: We made several improvements to the website.
examples.cn: 我们对网站做了几处改进。

examples.en: His health showed a slow improvement over the spring.
examples.cn: 他的健康在春天里慢慢好转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木扑入夫门特」——把破木门修好扑进夫家，是一大改善。

root: 古法语 prou（利益）→ emprower（使有利可图）→ improve + -ment（名词后缀）→ improvement；同族词有 improve、improved、improving、unimproved。

sensesIntro.en: Improvement names both the journey toward better and each single step taken on it.
sensesIntro.cn: improvement 既命名「变好」这一过程，也命名路上每一个具体的改进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old machine with a new part, suddenly quieter.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧机器换了新零件，声音一下子轻了。

branches.en: PROCESS LINE: the general movement upward.
branches.cn: 过程线：整体向上的变化。

branches.en: CHANGE LINE: each improvement can be counted.
branches.cn: 改动线：每处改进都能数出来。

branches.en: ROOM LINE: the phrase that keeps people working.
branches.cn: 余地线：让人继续努力的惯用语。

branches.en: HEALTH LINE: the body recovers on the same scale.
branches.cn: 健康线：身体也按同一尺度好转。

branches.en: CONTRAST: progress is wider, improvement is measurable.
branches.cn: 对照线：progress 更宽，improvement 可量化。

intro.en: The verb improve with the French noun ending for an act or its result.
intro.cn: 动词 improve 加法语名词词尾，表示动作或其结果。

latinIntro.en: The word is French in origin: prou, profit, gave emprower, and English added -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词出自法语：prou「利益」生出 emprower，英语再加 -ment。

items.example: It carries the sense of putting into a state.

definition_en: the state of not being able to do something
core_image: 手伸到一半停住，够不着那本书
scene: 想帮忙却使不上劲，最难受。He had to admit his inability to answer the question.
sceneCN: 这里 inability 是「无力、无法」（第 1 个义项：做不到某事的状态）；句意是他不得不承认自己答不上这个问题。

pos.zh: 名词：不能；无力；无能

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀，义为「能力」
换否定前缀，义为「不能的」

senses.title: Lack of power to do something
senses.definition: the fact of not being able to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做不到某事的状况
senses.example: He had to admit his inability to answer the question.
senses.exampleCN: 他不得不承认自己答不上这个问题。
senses.why: Latin in- is not and habilis means handy, so inability is literally not having the thing at hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表「不」，habilis 意为「顺手的」，所以 inability 字面就是「手里没有可用的东西」。

senses.title: Lack of a particular skill
senses.definition: a lack of the skill needed for a task
senses.definitionCN: 缺少完成某任务所需的技巧
senses.example: Her inability to swim kept her out of the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 她不会游泳，所以没能上船。
senses.why: The lack can be one skill rather than all power, and English says inability to swim, to read, to sleep.
senses.whyCN: 缺的可以只是某一项技能而不是全部本领，所以英语说 inability to swim、to read、to sleep。

senses.title: In law, lack of legal power
senses.titleCN: 无能力：法律上没有资格
senses.definition: in law, want of legal capacity to act
senses.definitionCN: 法律上缺少行为的资格
senses.example: The court considered the witness's inability to understand the oath.
senses.exampleCN: 法院考虑的是证人无法理解誓言的资格问题。
senses.why: Legal writing keeps the old sense of capacity, which is not about effort but about standing.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书保留「资格」这一旧义，它与努力无关，而与身份有关。

senses.title: Lack of means to pay
senses.definition: the state of not having the means, often money
senses.definitionCN: 缺少条件，常指缺钱
senses.example: Inability to pay is not the same as unwillingness.
senses.exampleCN: 无力支付不等于不愿意支付。
senses.why: The noun describes the absence of means, so it pairs naturally with money and resources.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词描述的是条件的缺席，所以天然与金钱、资源这类词搭配。

intro.en: Inability is in-, not, joined to ability, from Latin habilitas, aptness, from habilis, handy.
intro.cn: inability 是 in-「不」加 ability，后者来自拉丁语 habilitas「适合」，源于 habilis「顺手可用的」。

items.en: Habilis meant handy or easy to use, from habere, to hold.
items.cn: habilis 意为「顺手、好用」，来自 habere「持有」。

items.en: Habilitas named the quality of being fit for something.
items.cn: habilitas 指「适合做某事」的性质。

items.en: French ablete carried the sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 ablete 把这个意思带进英语。

items.en: Ability arrived in the fourteenth century, and inability followed.
items.cn: ability 在十四世纪进入英语，inability 随后而来。

items.en: The in- form is the plain way to refuse to do without.
items.cn: in- 形式是最平实的「做不到」的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with able and its prefixes; the near-meaning group separates inability, refusal and disability.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 able 与各前缀；近义组区分「不能」「不愿」与「残疾」。

entries.definition: The power or skill to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力」，去掉否定前缀。

entries.definition: Not able, the everyday adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不能的」，是最常用的形容词形式。

entries.definition: To make someone able to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够」。

entries.definition: Lack of legal or physical capacity, more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无能力」，更正式，多用于法律。

entries.definition: Refusal that comes from choice, not from lack of power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不愿意」，源自选择而非能力。

entries.definition: A lasting condition that limits activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「残疾」，指持续的身体限制。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the in- plus ability build, the reaching hand and the fixed to-do complement.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 in- 加 ability 的构词、伸手够不到的意象以及 to do 的固定补语。

normal.en: In- plus ability is simply the absence of the ability.
normal.cn: in- 加 ability 就是能力的缺席。

normal.en: Inability takes to plus a verb: inability to pay, inability to sleep.
normal.cn: inability 后接 to 加动词：inability to pay，inability to sleep。

normal.en: Unable is the adjective, inability the noun, ability the positive.
normal.cn: unable 形容词，inability 名词，ability 肯定形式。

normal.en: Enable is the opposite move: it gives the ability.
normal.cn: enable 是反向操作：把能力给出去。

normal.en: Inability to pay is a phrase you meet in every contract.
normal.cn: inability to pay 是合同里常见的说法。

abstract.en: Inability is not a fault; it is a boundary that can be described.
abstract.cn: 无能不是过错，只是一条可以被描述出来的边界。

abstract.en: What we call inability is often only inexperience wearing a different name.
abstract.cn: 所谓无能，常常只是「没经历过」换了个名字。

abstract.en: Knowing what you cannot do is the first form of skill.
abstract.cn: 知道自己不能做什么，是本领的第一种形式。

examples.en: His inability to hear the phone caused the delay.
examples.cn: 他没听见电话，才耽误了事情。

examples.en: The inability to pay rent forced them to move.
examples.cn: 无力支付房租，迫使他们搬家。

examples.en: She spoke about her inability to sleep with great honesty.
examples.cn: 她非常坦诚地谈到自己睡不着的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因恶比利提」——因为恶劣的条件，比利提不起来，就是没能力。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ habilitas（适合，来自 habilis 顺手的）→ inability；同族词有 ability、able、unable、enable、disable。

sensesIntro.en: Inability names every kind of absence of power: physical, skilled, legal and financial.
sensesIntro.cn: inability 命名各种力量缺席：身体上的、技能上的、法律上的和钱财上的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stopped mid-reach, just short of the book.
core.cn: 核心意象：手伸到一半停住，离那本书还差一点。

branches.en: POWER LINE: the plain absence of capacity.
branches.cn: 能力线：最平实的「做不到」。

branches.en: SKILL LINE: the gap is a missing technique.
branches.cn: 技能线：缺口是一项没学会的本领。

branches.en: LAW LINE: the law decides who may act.
branches.cn: 法律线：由法律决定谁有资格。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the means are absent, not the will.
branches.cn: 金钱线：缺的是条件，不是意愿。

branches.en: CONTRAST: inability differs from unwillingness.
branches.cn: 对照线：inability 与「不愿意」不同。

intro.en: A negating prefix on the noun for ability, with the whole able family around it.
intro.cn: 否定前缀加在表示能力的名词上，周围是整个 able 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, to hold, gave habilis and habilitas, and English built ability and inability on them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere「持有」生出 habilis 与 habilitas，英语在其上造出 ability 与 inability。

items.example: It negates the ability that follows.
The stem of ability and rehabilitation.
items.exampleCN: ability 与 rehabilitation 的词根。

items.example: It makes a noun of quality.
items.exampleCN: 它造出表示性质的名词。

definition_en: a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot, or to move very slowly
core_image: 大拇指的宽度：一格一格量过去
scene: 量布的时候不用尺，一只大拇指按着往前挪。The crack widened by an inch overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 inch 是「英寸」（第 1 个义项：长度单位，一英尺的十二分之一）；句意是那条裂缝一夜之间加宽了一英寸。

pos.zh: 名词：英寸；一点，少许
动词：缓慢移动，一点点挪动

collocations.phrase: give him an inch and he will take a mile

derivatives.zh: 动词过去式，义为「缓慢挪动」
现在分词，义为「一点点移动」

senses.title: A twelfth of a foot
senses.definition: a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot, about two and a half centimetres
senses.definitionCN: 长度单位，等于一英尺的十二分之一，约二点五厘米
senses.example: The crack widened by an inch overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那条裂缝一夜之间加宽了一英寸。
senses.why: The unit was once taken from the width of a thumb, so the word started as a body measure rather than a number.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位最早取的是大拇指的宽度，所以它起初是身体尺度，而不是抽象数字。

senses.title: A very small distance
senses.definition: a very small distance or amount
senses.definitionCN: 极小的距离或数量
senses.example: The car missed the post by inches.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车差几英寸就撞上柱子。
senses.why: Once a thumb width becomes a unit, the unit can measure any short gap, and it comes to mean almost nothing at all.
senses.whyCN: 拇指宽一旦成为单位，就什么小缝隙都用它量，于是它也就表示「几乎等于没有」。

senses.title: To move slowly and with effort
senses.titleCN: 缓慢挪动：一点一点地移
senses.definition: to move very slowly in small steps
senses.definitionCN: 以小步幅极慢地移动
senses.example: The line of cars inched along the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 车流沿着山路一点点往前挪。
senses.why: The verb borrows the noun: progress is measured one inch at a time, so moving that way is to inch.
senses.whyCN: 动词借用了名词：前进是按「一寸」来量的，所以那样移动就叫 inch。

senses.title: Complete in every part
senses.definition: used in every inch to mean completely
senses.definitionCN: 用于 every inch，表示完完全全
senses.example: She is every inch a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她完完全全是个老师的样子。
senses.why: If a thing is measured inch by inch and no gap is found, it is entirely what it claims to be, hence every inch.
senses.whyCN: 若一寸一寸量遍而没有空隙，它就彻底是它自称的那样，于是有 every inch。

senses.title: A narrow margin
senses.definition: a margin so narrow that failure was close
senses.definitionCN: 窄到几乎失败的地步
senses.example: He came within an inch of losing the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他差一点就输了这场官司。
senses.why: A single thumb width is the smallest gap the old measure could show, so any close escape is stated in inches.
senses.whyCN: 一个拇指宽是旧尺度能显示的最小间隙，所以任何险胜险败都用英寸来说。

senses.title: Rainfall or snow depth
senses.definition: the depth of rain or snow measured in inches
senses.definitionCN: 以英寸计的雨雪深度
senses.example: Two inches of snow fell before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前下了两英寸的雪。
senses.why: Depth is the most natural thing to measure in short units, so weather reports count precipitation in inches.
senses.whyCN: 深度最自然用短单位来量，所以天气预报用英寸来计降水量。

senses.title: Screen or waist measurement
senses.definition: the size of a screen or a waist given in inches
senses.definitionCN: 以英寸标出的屏幕或腰围尺寸
senses.example: The tablet has a ten inch screen.
senses.exampleCN: 这台平板有十英寸的屏幕。
senses.why: Manufacturers keep the old unit alive because a larger number sounds bigger, which is why inch survived metrification.
senses.whyCN: 厂商沿用旧单位，是因为数字更大听起来更大，这也是 inch 在公制化之后还活着的原因。

senses.title: To advance by small gains
senses.definition: to advance slowly but steadily towards a goal
senses.definitionCN: 朝目标缓慢而稳定地前进
senses.example: The two sides inched towards an agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 双方一点点地向协议靠近。
senses.why: The slow movement of the verb is applied to abstract progress, because bargaining also moves by tiny measured steps.
senses.whyCN: 动词的缓慢位移被用到抽象的进展上，因为谈判也是一小步一小步地挪。

intro.en: Inch descends from Latin uncia, a twelfth part, the same root that gave ounce.
intro.cn: inch 出自拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」，与 ounce 同源。

items.en: Uncia meant a twelfth part of anything, including weight and length.
items.cn: uncia 指任何东西的十二分之一，包括重量与长度。

items.en: Old English ynce borrowed the unit and the name together.
items.cn: 古英语 ynce 把单位和名称一起借了过来。

items.en: The spelling settled on inch while the length stayed a twelfth of a foot.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 inch，长度仍是一英尺的十二分之一。

items.en: Thumb width and barleycorn were quoted as the everyday basis of the unit.
items.cn: 十六世纪时人们常拿拇指宽与大麦粒作为该单位的日常依据。

items.en: Inch survives beside the metric system and turned into a verb of slow movement.
items.cn: inch 在公制旁边留存下来，并变成表示缓慢移动的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the uncia family; the near-meaning group places short units and slow movement side by side.
note.cn: 形近组是 uncia 词族；近义组并列短小的单位与缓慢的移动。

entries.definition: A unit of weight, also a twelfth of an older pound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「盎司」，出自同一个 uncia「十二分之一」。

entries.definition: The plural of the unit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，inch 的复数形式。

entries.definition: Moved very slowly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，义为「缓慢挪动」。

entries.definition: The metric unit closest in size to an inch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「厘米」，公制里与英寸大小最接近的单位。

entries.definition: A small part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一小部分」。

entries.definition: To move slowly and quietly, close to the verb sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「爬行、缓行」，接近其动词义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the uncia root, the thumb, and the fixed phrases built on the unit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 uncia 词根、大拇指以及建立在这个单位上的固定搭配。

normal.en: Inch and ounce are twins from Latin uncia: both name a twelfth part.
normal.cn: inch 与 ounce 是拉丁语 uncia 的双胞胎：都指十二分之一。

normal.en: Twelve inches make a foot, and the foot is the body part that anchors them.
normal.cn: 十二英寸是一英尺，而 foot 这个身体部位正是它们的落点。

normal.en: Inch by inch means slowly and steadily, never by leaps.
normal.cn: inch by inch 意为一点一点、稳稳地，绝不跳跃。

normal.en: Within an inch of means a near miss, and every inch means completely.
normal.cn: within an inch of 表示差一点，every inch 表示彻底。

normal.en: The verb inch keeps the same rhythm: motion measured in tiny steps.
normal.cn: 动词 inch 保持同样的节奏：以小步幅计量的移动。

abstract.en: A thumb is the first ruler a child owns.
abstract.cn: 大拇指是孩子手里的第一把尺。

abstract.en: Small units make progress visible; that is why the verb feels encouraging.
abstract.cn: 小单位让进展看得见，所以这个动词听起来让人受鼓舞。

abstract.en: Give an inch, take a mile: the unit measures how far politeness can go.
abstract.cn: 得寸进尺：这个单位也在衡量客气能走多远。

examples.en: The water rose an inch during the night.
examples.cn: 夜里水位涨了一英寸。

examples.en: Traffic inched forward for an hour.
examples.cn: 车流一点点挪了一个小时。

examples.en: She is every inch a professional.
examples.cn: 她彻头彻尾是个专业人士。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因此」——尺寸差一点，因此要一寸一寸重新量。

root: 拉丁语 uncia（十二分之一）→ 古英语 ynce → inch；同源词有 ounce，另有 foot 作为十二倍的换算基准。

sensesIntro.en: Inch begins as a body measure, then stretches to mean a tiny distance, a very close margin and a slow manner of moving.
sensesIntro.cn: inch 起初是身体尺度，随后延伸到极小的距离、极险的差距以及缓慢移动的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the width of a thumb laid down along cloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只大拇指沿着布面按下去量。

branches.en: MEASURE LINE: the unit for short lengths and depths.
branches.cn: 度量线：用于短长度与深度的单位。

branches.en: SMALLNESS LINE: a distance almost equal to nothing.
branches.cn: 微小线：几乎等于没有的距离。

branches.en: MOTION LINE: progress counted one step at a time.
branches.cn: 移动线：一步一步计量的前进。

branches.en: WHOLENESS LINE: measuring every part leaves no gap.
branches.cn: 整体线：每一寸都量过就没有空隙。

branches.en: CONTRAST: inch is a body measure, centimetre an abstract one.
branches.cn: 对照线：inch 是身体尺度，centimetre 是抽象尺度。

intro.en: A single Latin stem narrowed to one twelfth part, with no productive prefixes or suffixes of its own.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁词干收窄为「十二分之一」，自身没有能产的前后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin uncia, a twelfth, produced both inch and ounce without further change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」直接生出 inch 与 ounce，中间没有再加变化。

items.example: The stem behind inch and ounce.
items.exampleCN: inch 与 ounce 背后的词干。

items.meaningCN: 以 ch 结尾的复数

definition_en: something that happens, often something unpleasant or unusual
core_image: 平静水面突然落下一块石头
scene: 巡逻记录本上，每一条都写着时间和地点。Police are investigating a small incident near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 incident 是「事件」（第 1 个义项：发生的、多带负面色彩的事）；句意是警方正在调查车站附近的一起小事件。

pos.zh: 名词：事件；事变；插曲
形容词：附带的，有关的（多用于 incident to）

derivatives.zh: 带 co-「共同」，义为「同时发生的」

senses.title: An event that happens
senses.definition: a single event, usually one noticed because it is unusual
senses.definitionCN: 单个发生的事，通常因不寻常而被注意
senses.example: Police are investigating a small incident near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在调查车站附近的一起小事件。
senses.why: The Latin verb incidere means to fall upon, so an incident is something that falls on the flow of ordinary days.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 incidere 意为「落到……上面」，所以 incident 就是落到平常日子里的一件事。

senses.title: A violent or unpleasant event
senses.definition: a violent or disruptive event such as a fight or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 打斗、事故等带破坏性的事件
senses.example: The incident at the border lasted less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 边境上的那起冲突不到一分钟就结束了。
senses.why: Because the word marks what interrupts normal life, it slides toward the unpleasant events that interrupt it hardest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的是打断日常生活的事，所以最容易落在打断得最厉害的不愉快事件上。

senses.title: A small episode in a story
senses.definition: a minor episode inside a larger story or journey
senses.definitionCN: 较大故事或旅程中的小片段
senses.example: The trip was calm apart from one funny incident in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 旅程很平静，只有市集上一段滑稽插曲。
senses.why: Narrators need a word for one thing that happens along the way, and the falling-upon image fits a passing episode.
senses.whyCN: 叙述者需要一个词指路上发生的一件事，而「落到身上」的意象正适合一段过眼的插曲。

senses.title: Something that follows from another
senses.definition: a thing that arises from or depends on something else, as in incident to
senses.definitionCN: 由他事附带产生或依附的事，如 incident to
senses.example: The costs incident to the move were paid by the company.
senses.exampleCN: 搬迁附带产生的费用由公司支付。
senses.why: What falls upon an event from the outside is not its core but its accompaniment, and this legal sense keeps that old angle.
senses.whyCN: 从外面落到一件事上的东西不是它的核心而是它的附属，这个法律义保留的正是那个旧角度。

senses.title: A recorded case in reports
senses.definition: a case formally recorded by police, hospitals or safety officers
senses.definitionCN: 由警方、医院或安全员正式登记的一起
senses.example: The report counts nine incidents of theft in the car park.
senses.exampleCN: 报告统计了停车场发生的九起盗窃案。
senses.why: Record keeping needs countable single events, so the word becomes the official unit of trouble in a logbook.
senses.whyCN: 记录工作需要一个可数的单起事件，于是这个词成了台账里「出事一次」的官方单位。

senses.title: A diplomatic crisis
senses.titleCN: 外交事件：两国间的纠葛
senses.definition: an event that damages relations between states
senses.definitionCN: 损害国家之间关系的事件
senses.example: The two countries argued for weeks over the incident.
senses.exampleCN: 两国为那起事件争吵了数周。
senses.why: When a single happening harms politics between nations, the neutral word still fits: it falls suddenly onto a whole relationship.
senses.whyCN: 当一桩事件损害国家间的政治关系时，中性的 incident 依然合适：它突然落在整段关系上。

senses.title: Exposure to danger
senses.titleCN: 受险：遇到危险（多见于高级语域）
senses.definition: the fact of being exposed to danger or falling into an experience
senses.definitionCN: 遭遇危险或陷入某种经历的事实
senses.example: People were advised to wash after incident to the water.
senses.exampleCN: 人们被建议接触水后要清洗。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the physical one of falling into something, and this rare formal use still holds the image of bodies meeting an event.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是身体落到某物里，这个罕见而正式的说法仍保留着「身体遇上事件」的画面。

senses.title: A statistical happening
senses.titleCN: 发生的事件：统计中的一次
senses.definition: one occurrence counted in statistics of crime, illness or error
senses.definitionCN: 犯罪、疾病或差错统计中的一次发生
senses.example: Each incident is logged with the time and the staff number.
senses.exampleCN: 每一件都登记了时间和员工工号。
senses.why: Any process that must be audited breaks experience into countable happenings, and the statistical use is that same habit.
senses.whyCN: 凡须审计的流程都会把经历切成一次次可数的事件，统计用法就是这同一种习惯。

intro.en: Incident comes from Latin incidere, to fall upon: in- into plus cadere, to fall.
intro.cn: incident 出自拉丁语 incidere「落到……之上」：in-「进入」加 cadere「落下」。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, the root of accident, occasion and decay.
items.cn: cadere 意为「落下」，是 accident、occasion、decay 的词根。

items.en: Incidere meant to fall into or upon something.
items.cn: incidere 意为「落进、落到某事上」。

items.en: The participle incidens named whatever falls upon us.
items.cn: 分词 incidens 指落到我们身上的东西。

items.en: French incident passed the noun into English.
items.cn: 法语 incident 把这个名词带进英语。

items.en: English narrowed it to single events, often troubling ones.
items.cn: 英语把它收窄为单起事件，往往带麻烦意味。

note.en: The look-alike group is the cadere family; the near-meaning group separates incident from accident and event.
note.cn: 形近组是 cadere 词族；近义组区分「事件」「事故」与「大事」。

entries.definition: Something that happens by chance, often causing harm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事故」，同源但带 ad- 前缀。

entries.definition: By the way, as a minor point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「顺便说一句」。

entries.definition: Happening at the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「同时发生的」，带共同前缀。

entries.definition: Any happening, including planned ones.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、活动」，含事先安排的事。

entries.definition: A happening, usually counted in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发生的事情」，多用于统计。

entries.definition: One part of a longer series.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一段插曲」，用于更长序列中的一段。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the cadere root, the stone on still water and the logged report.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 cadere 词根、落进静水的石头以及登记在册的报告。

normal.en: In- plus cadere, to fall: an incident is what falls onto an ordinary day.
normal.cn: in- 加 cadere「落下」：incident 就是落到平常日子上的一件事。

normal.en: Incident, accident, occasion all share the falling root; only the prefixes differ.
normal.cn: incident、accident、occasion 共用「落下」词根，区别只在前缀。

normal.en: Without incident is the polite way to say nothing went wrong.
normal.cn: without incident 是「一路平安」的客气说法。

normal.en: Incidental is the adjective for costs that come along with a main thing.
normal.cn: incidental 是形容随主事附带而来的费用。

normal.en: Incidentally begins a sentence that is not the main point at all.
normal.cn: incidentally 引出的那句话，根本不是重点。

abstract.en: An incident is a stone; the day is the water that keeps its shape afterwards.
abstract.cn: 事件是石头，日子是水，事后水面上还留着圈。

abstract.en: A report turns an incident into a line with a time stamp.
abstract.cn: 一份报告把事件压成带时间的一行字。

abstract.en: Calling something an incident already hints that it should not have happened.
abstract.cn: 把一件事叫作 incident，本身就在暗示它本不该发生。

examples.en: The journey to the coast passed without incident.
examples.cn: 前往海岸的旅程一路平安。

examples.en: Police recorded three separate incidents that night.
examples.cn: 警方当晚记录了三起独立事件。

examples.en: It was an isolated incident, the manager insisted.
examples.cn: 经理坚持说那只是孤立事件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因事登场」——因为出了事，才登上了记录本。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ cadere（落下）→ incidere（落到身上）→ incidens → incident；同族词有 accident、coincident、incidental、occasion。

sensesIntro.en: Incident starts from the image of something falling on us, then covers any single happening, the unpleasant ones first.
sensesIntro.cn: incident 从「有东西落到我们身上」的意象出发，随后指任何单起事件，而其中最常被提起的是不愉快的那类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropping into still water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头落进平静的水面。

branches.en: EVENT LINE: any single happening, big or small.
branches.cn: 事件线：任何单起的事，无论大小。

branches.en: TROUBLE LINE: the word slides toward conflict and crisis.
branches.cn: 麻烦线：词义滑向冲突与危机。

branches.en: RECORD LINE: counted cases in logs and statistics.
branches.cn: 记录线：台账与统计里被计数的一起起。

branches.en: ATTACHMENT LINE: what falls on a thing from outside.
branches.cn: 附随线：从外面落到一件事上的东西。

branches.en: CONTRAST: accident stresses chance, incident stresses the happening itself.
branches.cn: 对照线：accident 强调偶然，incident 强调「发生了这件事」。

intro.en: A direction prefix, the root for falling, and the noun endings that grew from the participle.
intro.cn: 方向前缀、表示「落下」的词根，以及由分词长出的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin incidere, to fall upon, produced the participle incidens and the noun incident through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 incidere「落到身上」经分词 incidens 与法语生出名词 incident。

items.example: It marks the falling onto something.
The stem of accident and occasion.
items.exampleCN: accident 与 occasion 的词根。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun of the doer.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成表行为的名字。

definition_zh: 倾向；倾斜；使倾向于；斜坡
definition_en: to lean towards something, or to make someone likely to do or think something
core_image: 手背轻轻一偏，杯里的水就靠向一侧
scene: 端着一杯水走山路，水总往低的一边靠。Hot weather inclines people to stay indoors.
sceneCN: 这里 incline 是「使倾向于」（第 1 个义项：让某人容易做出某种选择）；句意是热天让人倾向于待在屋里。

pos.zh: 动词：倾向；使倾向于；倾斜
名词：斜坡，斜面

collocations.zh: 没有任何理由让他倾向于此

derivatives.zh: 带 re-「向后」，义为「向后靠、斜躺」
带 de-「向下」，义为「下降、婉拒」

senses.title: To make someone likely to act
senses.titleCN: 使倾向于：让人容易这样做
senses.definition: to make someone likely to do or choose something
senses.definitionCN: 让人容易做出或选择某件事
senses.example: Hot weather inclines people to stay indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 热天让人倾向于待在屋里。
senses.why: A tilted surface lets a ball roll one way, and the mind tilted by a cause rolls toward one choice, which is what the verb says.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜的面让球往一边滚，被某个原因弄偏的心也会往一个选择倒，动词说的正是这件事。

senses.title: To be likely in attitude
senses.titleCN: 倾向于：态度上偏向（常用 be inclined to）
senses.definition: to have a tendency to agree or to think in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 在态度上容易同意或持某种看法
senses.example: I am inclined to accept their offer.
senses.exampleCN: 我倾向于接受他们的提议。
senses.why: The passive form describes a mind already leaning, and the leaning is enough to report without committing as yet.
senses.whyCN: 被动形式描述一颗已经倾斜的心，而有了这个倾斜就足以报告，不必正式表态。

senses.title: To lean physically
senses.definition: to lean or slope to one side
senses.definitionCN: 向一侧歪斜或倾斜
senses.example: He inclined his head to hear her better.
senses.exampleCN: 他把头侧过去，好听清她说什么。
senses.why: The oldest sense is bodily: a body tips toward what it wants to reach, and everything else borrows that geometry.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是身体上的：身体往想够到的东西那边歪，其余用法都借用这套几何。

senses.title: A slope
senses.definition: a sloping surface, especially a steep one
senses.definitionCN: 倾斜的表面，尤指陡坡
senses.example: The path begins with a long incline.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路开头是一段长坡。
senses.why: A leaning line drawn in the ground is a slope, so the noun keeps the same picture as the verb.
senses.whyCN: 在地面上画出的斜线就是坡，所以名词与动词保留同一幅画面。

senses.title: A natural taste
senses.definition: a natural desire or liking
senses.definitionCN: 天生就有的愿望或喜好
senses.example: She showed an early incline towards painting.
senses.exampleCN: 她早年就显出对绘画的偏好。
senses.why: A taste is a habitual lean of attention, and the same root supplies inclination for that lasting tilt.
senses.whyCN: 喜好是长期的注意力偏斜，同一个词根就用 inclination 来指这种持久的倾斜。

senses.title: To turn the head or ear
senses.definition: to move the head or ear toward a sound
senses.definitionCN: 把头或耳朵转向声音的方向
senses.example: She inclined an ear to the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她侧过耳朵朝向门。
senses.why: Hearing is better at an angle, so the body tips, and the verb records this small deliberate tilt.
senses.whyCN: 侧一点听得更清，于是身体倾过去，这个动词记录的就是这个有意的小动作。

senses.title: To slope away from vertical
senses.definition: to slope away from the vertical
senses.definitionCN: 整体偏离竖直方向
senses.example: The old tower inclines slightly to the east.
senses.exampleCN: 那座古塔略微向东倾斜。
senses.why: When a whole structure leaves the plumb line, it inclines; the verb measures how far it has strayed from upright.
senses.whyCN: 整座建筑离开铅垂线就叫 incline，这个动词也在测量它歪了多少。

senses.title: To favour a judgement
senses.titleCN: 倾向于认为：让人容易下某种判断
senses.definition: to make a judgement likely in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 让某种判断更容易成立
senses.example: The evidence inclines me to believe him.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据让我倾向于相信他。
senses.why: Judgement is weighed on a tilted scale: evidence put on one side lowers it, and that lowering is what inclines the mind.
senses.whyCN: 判断是在倾斜的天平上称的：证据压到一侧，那一侧下沉，这种下沉就是让心倾斜。

senses.title: A geotechnical slope
senses.titleCN: 坡度：工程与地理中的坡
senses.definition: a slope measured in engineering or geography
senses.definitionCN: 工程与地理中计量的坡面
senses.example: The engineers checked the incline of the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查了隧道的坡度。
senses.why: Practice needs a name for the measured steepness of ground and shafts, so the noun serves as a technical term as well.
senses.whyCN: 实务需要给地面与竖井的陡度一个名字，于是这个名词也充当技术用语。

intro.en: Incline joins Latin in-, towards, to clinare, to lean, the same root as lean and cline.
intro.cn: incline 由拉丁语 in-「朝向」加 clinare「倾」组成，与 lean 同源。

items.en: Clinare meant to bend or lean, the source of recline and decline.
items.cn: clinare 意为「弯曲、倾」，是 recline 与 decline 的来源。

items.en: Inclinare meant to bend toward something.
items.cn: inclinare 意为「朝某物弯过去」。

items.en: The participle inclinatus described a body or mind already leaning.
items.cn: 分词 inclinatus 描述已倾斜的身体或心意。

items.en: French incliner carried the word into English use.
items.cn: 法语 incliner 把这个词带入英语。

items.en: Incline covers slopes, head tilts and habits of mind at once.
items.cn: 现代英语的 incline 同时覆盖坡面、侧头和思维习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group is the clinare family; the near-meaning group lines up lean, prefer and tendency.
note.cn: 形近组是 clinare 词族；近义组并列「倾向」「偏爱」与「趋势」。

entries.definition: To slope down, and so to fall or to refuse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「下降、婉拒」，同源带 de-「向下」。

entries.definition: To lean back in a seat.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「向后靠」，同源带 re-「向后」。

entries.definition: A leaning of mind, a liking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倾向、喜好」。

entries.definition: To be likely to do something over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「往往会」，强调长期趋势。

entries.definition: To like one thing more than another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「更喜欢」，是明确选择。

entries.definition: To slope or to favour one side in plain English.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「倾斜、偏向」，最朴素的说法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the clinare root, the cup of water and the fixed patterns with inclined.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 clinare 词根、那杯水以及 inclined 的固定句式。

normal.en: Incline, decline, recline all lean: toward, down, back.
normal.cn: incline、decline、recline 都是「倾」：向前、向下、向后。

normal.en: Be inclined to do is the polite way to state a likely choice.
normal.cn: be inclined to do 是客气地说出可能选择的方式。

normal.en: Incline towards works with both places and opinions.
normal.cn: incline towards 既能接地方，也能接观点。

normal.en: The noun a steep incline names the slope itself, not the act.
normal.cn: 名词 a steep incline 指坡本身，不指倾斜这个动作。

normal.en: Inclination is the lasting version: a taste rather than a single lean.
normal.cn: inclination 是持久版：是喜好，不是一时的倾。

abstract.en: A mind that leans is easier to move than one standing straight.
abstract.cn: 已经倾斜的心比直立的更容易推动。

abstract.en: Every slope decides the direction of the next rain.
abstract.cn: 每一道坡都决定了下一场雨往哪流。

abstract.en: To be inclined is to have already started, without having yet said yes.
abstract.cn: inclined 意味着已经开始，只是还没答应。

examples.en: Long hours indoors incline children to feel sleepy.
examples.cn: 长时间待在室内会让孩子容易犯困。

examples.en: I am inclined to agree with the second report.
examples.cn: 我倾向于同意第二份报告。

examples.en: The road climbs a gentle incline for two miles.
examples.cn: 这条路有两英里的缓坡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因客来」——因为客人来了，椅子被斜着摆开一点。

root: 拉丁语 in-（朝向）+ clinare（倾斜）→ inclinare → incline；同族词有 decline、recline、inclination、lean。

sensesIntro.en: Incline begins as a physical lean and spreads to slopes and to the mind that leans toward one choice.
sensesIntro.cn: incline 从身体的倾斜出发，扩展到地面上的坡，再扩展到偏向某个选择的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tilting, so the water inside leans to one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：手微微一倾，杯里的水靠向一侧。

branches.en: MIND LINE: a cause tilts the choice or the judgement.
branches.cn: 心智线：某个原因让选择或判断倾斜。

branches.en: BODY LINE: heads, ears and towers leave the upright.
branches.cn: 身体线：头、耳朵与塔离开竖直方向。

branches.en: SLOPE LINE: the leaning line drawn on the ground.
branches.cn: 坡面线：画在地面上的斜线。

branches.en: HABIT LINE: a lasting lean becomes a taste.
branches.cn: 习惯线：持久的倾斜变成喜好。

branches.en: CONTRAST: incline is softer than decide, stronger than consider.
branches.cn: 对照线：incline 比 decide 软，比 consider 硬。

intro.en: A direction prefix and the root for leaning, with the noun family it produced.
intro.cn: 方向前缀与表示「倾」的词根，以及它派生出的名词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin inclinare, to bend toward, gave incline and inclination, and shares clinare with decline and recline.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inclinare「朝某处弯」生出 incline 与 inclination，并与 decline、recline 共用 clinare。

items.example: It points the leaning at a target.
items.exampleCN: 它把倾斜指向某个目标。

items.example: The stem of recline and decline.
items.exampleCN: recline 与 decline 的词根。

items.example: It keeps the Latin verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了拉丁动词的形态。

items.example: It names the state of leaning.
